media.title: Face the Rising Sun

tool_config.idea: Find east by turning Manu on the screen until the rising Sun is in front of him, then read the direction of his left hand, his right hand and behind him from that one fact. This is the free first try of the chapter, so it asks and shows; the video that follows names the rule.
tool_config.title: Face the Rising Sun
tool_config.screen: The sunrise field board on the trip desk, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. A round green hill field fills the middle of the board and is the largest thing on screen. Manu, the boy of your maths book, stands in the middle of the field, seen from behind, with both arms stretched out to the sides. At the start the rising Sun is on his right. The rising Sun is a large bright disc fixed low on the horizon above the soft hills, and it never moves when Manu turns. A small arrow grows from his chest to show where he faces, and an arrow grows from each hand, one from his left hand and one from his right hand. Four empty tag slots sit at the end of the front arrow, the left hand arrow, the right hand arrow and behind him, and they turn with him. A tray under the field holds four word tags: North, East, South and West. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with seven progress dots under it. The compass card, a small square card with N at the top, E in red on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left as in your maths book, stays hidden until the practice cards are done and then shows in the top right corner. Controls: Turn left and Turn right (a quarter turn each, with a gentle animation); tap a word tag and then tap a slot to put the tag there, and tap a tag that is in a slot to take it out; Check; Hint; Retry (clears the tags of this card); Reset (returns Manu to his starting turn and clears all the tags); Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: a line Where is the Sun now? that says in front of Manu, on his left, on his right or behind him, a count of the quarter turns made, and a card number out of 7.
feedback: Turn left and Turn right move Manu a quarter turn each time. The Sun stays where it is, so the line Where is the Sun now? changes as he turns, for example from on his right to in front of him.
When the Sun is not in front of Manu on card 1 the tool says: The Sun is not in front of Manu yet. Turn him again.
When he faces the Sun the tool says: Manu faces the rising Sun, so the tag in front of him is East. The slot lights up soft green when its tag is right.

A wrong tag shows a soft amber note and never a red cross, for example: Look again. Face the Sun yourself and stretch out your left arm. Which direction does it point to? The tool names the right tag only after the second try.
After card 3 the tool says: Manu faces north, so his left hand points West now. A hand does not always point the same way. It depends on which way Manu faces.
The last card is an open challenge: the tool shows what the tags say and lets the student change them, and the video that follows names the rule.
tool_config.done_when: Manu has been turned to the rising Sun, the tags East, North, South and West have been placed for his front, his left hand, his right hand and behind him, the compass card has been opened and compared, and the two questions from your maths book have been answered with the tags.

placement.where: last concept of the topic, after its teaching and worked examples

challenges: Card 1: turn Manu until the rising Sun is straight in front of him. Which direction tag goes in front of him? Answer: East, because the Sun rises in the east.
Card 2: with Manu facing the Sun, tag his left hand and his right hand. Answer: North for his left hand and South for his right hand.

Card 3 (practice values): turn Manu to face north, one quarter turn to the left from the Sun. Which direction does his right hand point to, and which his left hand? Answer: his right hand points to the East and his left hand to the West. The Sun is on his right now, and his hands point in other directions than before, so a hand does not always point the same way.
Card 4: turn Manu back to face the rising Sun, one quarter turn to the right, and tag the direction behind him. Answer: West, which is opposite to East.

Card 5: open the compass card and compare. Manu faces East, so on the card he looks to the right. Which tags match the card? Answer: all four. East is in front of him on the right of the card, North is at the top on his left hand, South is at the bottom on his right hand and West is on the left behind him.

Challenge: 'Manu is facing the rising Sun. That direction is ___. His left hand is pointing in the ___ direction. His right hand is pointing in the ___ direction.' Turn Manu to the Sun and fill the three tags. Answer: East, North, South.

Challenge: 'which way is west?' Tag the direction that is neither in front of Manu nor on a hand. Answer: West is behind Manu, opposite to the rising Sun. Next stop: the rule that names the four directions.

hint_ladder.text: Where is the Sun on the screen? Turn Manu until the Sun is straight in front of him.
The Sun rises in the east. When Manu faces the Sun, he faces east. Now think about his hands: which side is each hand on?
Manu faces east. Face the Sun yourself and stretch out your left arm: it points north. Then stretch out your right arm: it points south.
The tool turns Manu to the Sun and puts East in front of him, North on his left hand, South on his right hand and West behind him. Then a similar card follows for you to try.

student_does: Look at the picture of the story again: the Siberian Crane that flies all the way from Siberia, the four little chicks of the poem that fly from east to west and from north to south, and Manu standing on the hill with his arms stretched out. Read the line: Human beings also keep track of directions. One of the ways is by facing the rising Sun. Then turn Manu until he faces the rising Sun, and press Next.

Turn Manu until the Sun is in front of him and tag that direction, tag the direction of his left hand and of his right hand, turn him to face north (practice values) and tag the hands again, turn him back to the Sun and tag the direction behind him, then open the compass card and compare.

Manu's own lines from your maths book, unchanged, as an open challenge: Manu is facing the rising Sun. That direction is ___. His left hand is pointing in the ___ direction. His right hand is pointing in the ___ direction. Then: which way is west? Fill the tags and read what the tool shows. The video that follows names the rule.

media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Face the Rising Sun
B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M1.S1.T1.C2.2D1
- Tool type: Exploration (the free first try, right after the story video)
- Textbook source: Maps and Locations, the opening activity: Manu facing the rising Sun, and the two questions repeated in Star Challenges 1 and 2. No numbers (developer only).
C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student finds east by turning to face the rising Sun, then names the directions of Manu's left hand, right hand and back from that one fact.
- Out of scope: reading a map, using a compass in the field, directions between the four, how birds find their way.
D. TOOL DESCRIPTION
1. Opening Screen
- A sunrise meadow seen from above (photo-style grass and sky). Manu, the boy of the opening story, stands at the centre of a round grass field, facing the top, both arms stretched out. At the right edge a bright Sun disc sits low over blue hills, its rays lying across the grass: the Sun is on Manu's right.
- Instruction line: "Turn Manu to face the rising Sun."
- The child is invited to tap one of the two big round turn arrows beside Manu's feet.
2. Scene and Objects
- Manu: a flat drawing seen from above and a little behind (round head, black hair, cream shirt, arms out, small shoes at the front), about 15 percent of the stage height. He turns on the spot, a quarter turn in half a second.
- The Sun: a flat glowing disc that never moves. Its caption (Activities 1 and 2 only) reads "The Sun is: on his right", then "in front of Manu", "behind him" or "on his left" after each turn.
- Arrows (from Activity 2): short arrows grow from Manu's chest (front), each hand and behind him, each ending in an empty dashed circle, a tag slot. They turn with Manu.
- Tag tray along the bottom: "North", "East", "South", "West". Two big round buttons, "Turn left" and "Turn right", with curved arrows, beside Manu's feet.
- Compass card (N top, E in red right, S bottom, W left): hidden until Activity 6, then in the top right corner. Before that the stage shows no direction letters (top is north, right east, bottom south, left west).
- One goal chip at the top shows the current goal.
3. Main Interaction
- Tap a turn arrow (or drag Manu round, snapping to a quarter): one quarter turn per tap. Tap a tag then a slot (or drag it); tap a tag in a slot to return it; one tag per slot.
- Any turn returns all tags to the tray, because the slots turn with Manu: "Manu turned, so his hands now point to other directions. Tag them again."
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" and the main button "Check", which becomes "Next" when the goal chip is green. Reset restarts the activity.
4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided). Goal line: "Turn Manu to face the rising Sun." Goal chip: "Face the Sun". Setup: Manu faces the top, the Sun is on his right, caption on, no arrows. Guess: the child taps the turn arrow they think brings the Sun in front of him, right or left; this tap is the guess. Result: after "Turn right" the rays brighten and the chip turns green with a bounce. Why line: "One quarter turn to the right, and the Sun is in front of Manu. He is facing the rising Sun." If the child turned left first, they keep turning until the Sun is in front; the line is then "Manu is facing the rising Sun." Help: guided, the caption changes after every turn.
- Activity 2 (guided). Goal line: "Which direction is in front of Manu?" Goal chip: "Front: ?", then "Front: East". Setup: Manu faces the Sun; only the front arrow and slot show; caption "in front of Manu". Guess: the child places a tag in the front slot and presses Check. Result: East turns green and bounces. Why line: "The Sun rises in the east, so the direction in front of Manu is east." Help: guided, a dotted ray joins the Sun and the front slot.
- Activity 3 (guided). Goal line: "Tag Manu's left hand and right hand." Goal chip: "Hands: ? ?". Setup: East stays in front; the hand arrows grow, labelled "left hand" and "right hand". Guess: the child is invited to face the Sun and stretch out their own left arm, then places two tags and presses Check. Result: North on the left hand and South on the right hand turn green. Why line: "Facing east, his left hand points north and his right hand points south." Help: guided, labels printed.
- Activity 4 (independent). Goal line: "Which direction is behind Manu?" Goal chip: "Behind: ?". Setup: East, North and South stand in their slots as plain grey words; the behind arrow grows; no labels, no caption. Guess: the child places a tag and presses Check. Result: West turns green. Why line: "West is behind Manu, opposite to east." Help: independent.
- Activity 5 (independent). Goal line: "Turn Manu to face north. Then tag his hands." Goal chip: "Face north". Setup: Manu faces the Sun, slots empty, no captions. Guess: the child taps Turn left or Turn right, the way they think Manu must turn to face north (his left hand pointed north in Activity 3). Result: after one quarter turn to the left the strip says "Manu faces north." and North fills the front slot; the child tags his right hand East and his left hand West. Why line: "Manu faces north, so his right hand points east, where the Sun is, and his left hand points west. A hand does not always point the same way." Help: independent.
- Activity 6 (independent). Goal line: "Match Manu to the compass card." Goal chip: "Match the card". Setup: Manu turns back to face the Sun by himself; the compass card opens in the corner with a small Manu at its centre and a short arrow from his chest. Guess: the child drags the arrow tip to the letter they think Manu faces. Result: the arrow snaps to E and the four tags show round the small Manu: East front, North left, South right, West behind. Why line: "Manu faces east, the right side of the card. North is at the top, on his left hand. South is at the bottom, on his right hand. West is on the left, behind him." Help: independent.
- Star Challenges: see section 7.
5. Mathematical Understanding
- Only the rising Sun is fixed. Facing it means facing east, so the left hand is north, the right hand south and the back west. Left and right turn with Manu; the four directions stay put.
- The rules to say at the end are the Remember lines of section 7.
6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the slot or chip turns green, the tag bounces gently, the strip shows the why line.
- Mistake: turns left in Activity 1 -> red strip, small shake: "The Sun is behind Manu now. Turn him the other way." The caption pulses.
- Mistake: a wrong front tag -> "Look at the Sun. It is straight in front of Manu. Which direction does the rising Sun come from?" After a second wrong tag: "The Sun rises in the east. Put the East tag in front of Manu."
- Mistake: West for the left hand (a hand always points west) -> "A hand does not always point west. Face the Sun yourself and stretch out your left arm. Which way does it point?" The left-hand arrow pulses. Hands swapped -> "You may have swapped the hands. Face the Sun yourself and stretch out your left arm first."
- Mistake: East behind Manu -> "East is in front of Manu. Behind him is the opposite way."
- Mistake: Activity 5, turns right (Manu faces south) -> "Manu faces south now. North is the way his left hand pointed when he faced the Sun. Turn him that way." A wrong tag for the right hand -> "The Sun has not moved: it is on Manu's right. Which direction is the Sun in?"
- Mistake: a wrong letter in Activity 6 -> "Manu faces the Sun, and the Sun is on the right of the stage. Which letter is on the right of the card?" Check with an empty slot -> "Put a tag in every empty circle first."
- Hint button, 3 levels: (1) words, for example "Where is the Sun? Turn Manu until the Sun is straight in front of him."; (2) visual: the Sun glows and a dotted ray joins it to Manu or to the slot to fill; (3) almost the answer: in Activity 1 the tool turns Manu one quarter turn right ("Now the Sun is in front of Manu. Press Check."); later "The Sun rises in the east. Facing east, your left arm points north and your right arm points south." and the first tag is placed.
- Edge cases: two turns put the Sun behind Manu; nothing can be dropped while Manu is turning.
7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Manu is facing the rising Sun. That direction is ___. His left hand is pointing in the ___ direction. His right hand is pointing in the ___ direction." Goal chip: "Fill the three blanks". Setup: Manu already faces the Sun; the three blanks are the front, left-hand and right-hand slots; no captions, no card. Guess: the child fills all three and presses Check. Success: East, North and South turn green. Why line: "Facing the Sun means facing east. His left hand points north and his right hand points south."
- Star Challenge 2 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "which way is west?" Goal chip: "Find west". Setup: the three green tags stay; the four arrow ends can be tapped. Guess: the child taps the arrow end they think points west. Success: the behind arrow takes the West tag with a bounce. Why line: "West is behind Manu, opposite to east." A tap on the front -> "That is east, where the Sun rises. West is the opposite way." A tap on a hand -> "That hand points north or south. West is opposite to east."
- End screen (confetti once): "Well done!" Remember: "Facing the rising Sun means facing east." "When you face east, your left hand points north, your right hand points south and west is behind you." "Left and right turn with you. North, east, south and west stay where they are." Think and talk: "If Manu turns his back on the rising Sun, which direction is he facing?" Button: "Start again".
8. Assets and Language
- Images: photo-style grass, sunrise sky and blue hills; the Sun disc (code glow); Manu as one flat drawing from above; tags, dashed circles, turn arrows and the compass card (code). English.

media.title: The crane and the four little chicks
media.context: Concept image for the hook, Four Little Chicks and the Siberian Crane. It draws the opener of your maths book, the crane that flies from Siberia and the four little chicks of the poem, with the compass rose, and it explains nothing about how birds find their way.
media.composition: Over two hills, one large white crane at the left leads four small yellow chicks in a loose line to the right, all flying to the left; a compass card sits in the top right corner.
media.description: A white Siberian Crane and four small yellow chicks flying to the left over two hills, with a compass card in the top right corner.
media.source_figure: A Siberian Crane with four small chicks in flight over hills, and a compass rose with N at the top, E in red on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left.
media.teaching_notes: Let the student look at the birds and the compass and wonder how a bird, or a person, keeps track of directions. Say no answer: your maths book does not explain how birds find their path, so it stays a question to wonder about. The slip to watch: taking the picture as a fact about bird journeys when it only sets the story.

topics.summary: A Siberian Crane flies all the way from Siberia to India, and four little chicks fly from east to west and from north to south. People keep track of directions too. Try turning Manu to face the rising Sun.

content.text:
I visited the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary in Rajasthan and saw an amazing bird called the Siberian Crane!
Wow! Do you know that these birds fly all the way from Siberia, a very cold place, to India?
I wonder how they find their path.
Four Little Chicks of a bird set out to fly,
Spreading their wings they all flew high.
They flew away from East to West,
flew North to South, without any rest.
As they flew and explored the land,
finally, they returned home, hand in hand.
With their mother, they had so much to share,
Our home is the best, beyond compare!

Manu stands on a grassy hill in the morning with his arms stretched out.

content.text:
Worked example: Lali faces the rising Sun on the school ground. She then turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. Which direction is she facing now, and which direction is behind her?
1. Lali faces the rising Sun. The rising Sun is in the east, so she faces east.
2. Facing east, her left hand points north and her right hand points south.
3. She turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. That is north, so she now faces north.
4. Behind her is the opposite of north. North and south are opposite directions, so south is behind her.
5. Check: north is at the top of the compass rose and south is at the bottom, so they are opposite directions.
Answer: She is facing north, and south is behind her

tool_config.screen: Three boards on the trip desk, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. The main board shows the bird-watching camp seen from above, as in your maths book: a grey road that curves from the top down to the bottom left, a lake with four ducks in the lower middle, four white tents with small red flags (one on the left of the road, one near the top on the right of the road, one just above the lake and one below the lake) and many green and yellow trees. The camp is the largest thing on screen. Two more boards slide in when a card needs them: the girl's room as in your maths book, with the girl, the window, the bed, the cupboard and the bedside table, and a small playground with a swing at the top left, a slide at the top right, a sandpit at the bottom left and a seesaw at the bottom right (practice values). The compass card, a small square card with N at the top, E in red on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left, sits in the top right corner of every board. A movable compass cross, a small round card with two diagonal lines through its centre, splits the picture around it into four zones: north above, south below, east on the right and west on the left. When the cross rests on a thing, the four zones are tinted softly and each zone shows its letter at the edge. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with seven progress dots under it, and a clue strip under it shows the clue being worked on. A pen tray holds a blue, a green, a purple and a yellow pen, and one spare tent waits beside the camp board. On the room board a small tray holds the word tags North, East, South and West, and a notes card with four lines, East, West, North and South, takes the names of things in the student's own room. Controls: drag the compass cross onto a thing; tap a thing to read its zone; tap a tent and then a pen to colour it, and tap the tent again to clear its colour; drag the spare tent onto the board; drag a word tag next to a name in the room list; type on the notes card; Check; Hint; Retry (clears the colours, tags or tent of this card); Reset (restores the board); Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: a zone line that says, after a tap, which zone of the cross the tapped thing is in, for example The slide is in the east zone of the cross; a count of tents coloured out of 4; and a card number out of 7.
feedback: When the cross rests on a thing the four zones tint and the zone line says where a tapped thing is, for example: The slide is in the east zone of the cross. The swing is in the west zone of the cross when the cross is on the slide.
A tent coloured to a clue clicks in with a soft chime and the clue strip says why, for example: The tent closest to the lake is the one just above it. That tent is green.
A wrong colour shows a soft amber note and never a red cross, for example: Which tent is west of the road? West is to the left on the picture. The tool names the right tent only after the second try.

A tag dropped next to a name in the room list is read at once, for example: The window is on the back wall, above the girl: north. A tag between two directions gets the note: This thing sits between two directions. Name the nearest one.
The spare tent turns green when it stands to the right of the lake, with the note: This tent is east of the lake. A tent anywhere else slides back with: East is to the right on the picture.
Open items, the tent to the east of the lake, the room list, the drawing and the names, are never marked wrong: the tool says Your answer may differ and offers Next.
tool_config.done_when: The compass cross has been moved onto the lake, onto a playground thing and onto the slide with the zones read correctly, the four tents are coloured by the four clues, a tent stands to the east of the lake, the room list has a direction for each thing, and the notes card has a name for each of the four directions.

placement.where: last concept of the topic, after its teaching and worked examples

challenges: Card 1: put the compass cross on the lake. Which tent is to the north of the lake and which tent is to the south of it? Answer: the tent just above the lake is to its north and the tent below the lake is to its south.

Card 2 (practice values): on the playground board put the cross on the swing. Which thing is east of the swing? Then put the cross on the sandpit. Which thing is north of the sandpit? Answer: the slide is east of the swing, and the swing is north of the sandpit.

Card 3 (practice values): put the cross on the slide. In which direction is the swing from the slide? Answer: west. The slide is east of the swing, so the swing is west of the slide. Seen from the other thing, the direction is the opposite one.

Challenge: 'Children are at a bird-watching camp. Read the clues and colour the tents in the camp accordingly. The tent to the west of the road is blue. The tent closest to the lake is green. The tent north of the green tent is purple. The tent south of the lake is yellow.' Answer: blue is the tent on the left of the road, green is the tent just above the lake, purple is the tent above the green tent near the top, and yellow is the tent below the lake.

Challenge: 'Now, draw a tent to the east of the lake.' Drag the spare tent onto the board. Answer: sample answer, the tent goes on the ground to the right of the lake. Any place to the right of the lake is right. Your answer may differ.

Challenge: 'Write the directions of the following in relation to the girl. Window ___ Bed ___ Cupboard ___ Bedside table ___' Drag the tags next to the names. Answer: sample answer, window north, bed east, cupboard west, bedside table south. The cupboard and the bedside table sit between two directions, so we name the nearest one. Your answer may differ.

Challenge: 'Make a drawing of your room and locate the direction in which different things have been placed in relation to you standing at the centre of the room. Make the direction arrow for your room.' Then: 'Write the names of the things that are placed in the following directions. East ___ West ___ North ___ South ___' Draw on paper, then type the names on the notes card. Answer: sample answer, in a sample room the bed is in the east, the cupboard in the west, the window in the north and the door in the south. To find north in your own room, face the rising Sun, which is east: north is on your left hand. Your answer may differ.

hint_ladder.text: Where is the compass cross now? Which thing is it resting on?
Which zone is the thing in? Above the cross is north, below is south, on the right is east and on the left is west.
Find the thing the clue talks about, rest the cross on it, and look at which tent lies in the zone the clue names.
The tool colours the first tent for you: the tent closest to the lake, just above it, turns green. Then a similar clue follows for you to try.

student_does: Look at the compass card and remember: facing the rising Sun is facing east, and on every picture N is at the top. Put the compass cross on the lake. Which tent is to its north?

With the cross on the lake, name the tent to its north and the tent to its south; on the playground (practice values) put the cross on the swing and find the thing to its east, on the sandpit and find the thing to its north, and on the slide and find where the swing is from it.

Your maths book's own items, unchanged. media.instructions_for_student: The student says the direction of a thing from another thing or from a person on a picture with a compass, and sees that if A is east of B then B is west of A.
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Direction Clues
B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M1.S4.T4.C11.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity
- Textbook source: Maps and Locations, Bird Watching (colour four tents by clues, draw a tent east of the lake) and Map of a Room (directions from the girl, your own room with a direction arrow, names in the four directions). No numbers (developer only).
C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student says the direction of one thing from another thing or from a person on a picture with a compass, and places things in a given direction.
- Out of scope: in-between directions, distances, routes.
D. TOOL DESCRIPTION
1. Opening Screen
- A school ground seen from above on a photo-style grass texture: a white flagpole at the centre; a library with a blue roof above it, a canteen with a red roof below it, a green cricket net to its left and a round blue water tank to its right, all the same distance away. The compass card is in the top right corner; a round compass cross waits in a tray at the bottom left.
- Instruction line: "Which thing is north of the flagpole? Make a guess."
- The child is invited to tap one of the four things.
2. Scene and Objects
- Compass card on every board: N top, E in red right, S bottom, W left.
- Compass cross: a round card (10 percent of the stage width) with two thin diagonal lines and a centre dot. Dropped on a thing it snaps there and four wedges tint: north above, south below, east right, west left. In Activities 1 and 2 each wedge prints its letter at the stage edge.
- Camp board (Star Challenges 1 and 2), as in the book, from above: a grey road curving from the top to the bottom left; a lake with four ducks in the lower middle; four white tents with red flags (one left of the road, one near the top right of the road, one just above the lake, one below it); trees. Four pens (blue, green, purple, yellow), a spare tent at the bottom right, four clue chips along the top.
- Room board (Star Challenge 3), as in the book, in perspective: the girl near the back wall, a window on the back wall behind her, a cupboard on the back wall to her left, a bed on the right, a round bedside table with a glass and a bottle in front of the bed. Name boxes "Window", "Bed", "Cupboard", "Bedside table" with empty dashed boxes; word tags "North", "East", "South", "West".
- My room board (Star Challenge 4): a wooden-floor plan with a dot "You" at the centre; eight cut-outs (bed, cupboard, window, door, table, chair, bookshelf, sofa); a direction-arrow card with four empty spots and chips N, E, S, W; four lines "East ___", "West ___", "North ___", "South ___" with dashed boxes and a chip "nothing here"; a tip chip: "To find north in your room: face the rising Sun. That is east. North is on your left hand."
- One goal chip at the top shows the current goal.
3. Main Interaction
- Drag the cross onto a thing: it snaps and tints; tap a thing and the strip names its wedge. Tap a tent then a pen to colour it. Drag the spare tent, a word tag (reusable) or a cut-out (off the plan to remove it).
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" and the main button "Check", which becomes "Next" when the goal chip is green. Reset restores the board.
4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided). Goal line: "Put the compass cross on the flagpole. Which thing is north of it?" Goal chip: "North of the flagpole". Guess: the child taps the thing they think is north, then drags the cross onto the flagpole. Result: the cross lands on the flagpole, the north wedge tints, the library glows green with a bounce. Why line: "The library is in the north zone, above the flagpole. The library is north of the flagpole." Help: guided, the north wedge pulses.
- Activity 2 (guided). Goal line: "Now find the thing that is west of the flagpole." Goal chip: "West of the flagpole". Setup: the cross stays on the flagpole; wedges tint only after a tap. Guess: the child taps the thing they think is west. Result: the cricket net glows green. Why line: "The cricket net is in the west zone, to the left of the flagpole, so it is west of the flagpole."
- Activity 3 (independent). Goal line: "Move the cross to the water tank. From the water tank, which direction is the cricket net?" Goal chip: "Net from the tank". Setup: the library and the canteen fade out; no zone letters. Guess: before moving the cross, the child taps a letter on the compass card. Result: the net is in the west wedge and W glows green. Why line: "From the water tank, the cricket net is in the west zone, so it is west of the tank."
- Activity 4 (independent). Goal line: "The library is north of the flagpole. From the library, which direction is the flagpole?" Goal chip: "Flagpole from the library". Setup: all four things are back, no letters. Guess: the child taps a letter on the compass card. Result: the cross is on the library, the flagpole is in the south wedge, S glows green. Why line: "The library is north of the flagpole, so the flagpole is south of the library. North and south are opposite."
- Star Challenges: see section 7.
5. Mathematical Understanding
- With N at the top, above is north, below is south, right is east and left is west. A direction is said from somewhere: the water tank is east of the flagpole, but from the tank the flagpole is west.
- The rules to say at the end are the Remember lines of section 7.
6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the thing or tent turns green with a gentle bounce and the strip shows the why line.
- Mistake: east and west mixed up -> red strip, small shake: "West is on the left of the compass card. Look to the left of the flagpole." W pulses. Activity 4, the same direction from both things -> "From the library you look the other way. If the library is north of the flagpole, the flagpole is south of the library."
- Mistake: Challenge 1, wrong tent for blue -> "West is to the left. Which tent is on the left of the road?" For green -> "Closest to the lake means nearest to the water." For purple -> "North is up. Find the green tent first, then look above it."
- Mistake: Challenge 2, left of the lake -> "East is to the right on this picture. Move the tent to the other side of the lake."
- Mistake: Challenge 3, a wrong tag for the window -> "The window is on the back wall, behind the girl. Look up the picture, towards the top of the compass."
- Hint button, 3 levels: (1) words: "Where is the thing you are asked about? From which thing or person are you looking?"; (2) visual: the cross jumps onto the thing or person you look from and the wedges tint; (3) almost the answer: the correct wedge pulses (Challenge 1: the first tent turns green).
- Open items (the tent, the room, your own room) are never marked wrong.
7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Children are at a bird-watching camp. Read the clues and colour the tents in the camp accordingly." Clue chips: "The tent to the west of the road is blue." "The tent closest to the lake is green." "The tent north of the green tent is purple." "The tent south of the lake is yellow." Goal chip: "Colour 4 tents". Guess: the child colours all four tents and presses Check; nothing is said before Check. Success: the tent left of the road is blue, the one just above the lake green, the one above it near the top purple, the one below the lake yellow; each clue chip turns green with its why line: "West is left: the tent on the left of the road is blue." "The tent just above the lake is closest to it: green." "North is up: the tent above the green tent is purple." "South is down: the tent below the lake is yellow."
- Star Challenge 2 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Now, draw a tent to the east of the lake." Goal chip: "A tent east of the lake". Guess: the child drags the spare tent where they choose and presses Check. Success: the tent stands on the ground inside the east wedge of an invisible cross on the lake and turns green: "This tent is east of the lake, on its right side. Your answer may differ: any place to the right of the lake is right."
- Star Challenge 3 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Write the directions of the following in relation to the girl. Window ___ Bed ___ Cupboard ___ Bedside table ___" Goal chip: "Directions from the girl". Guess: the child drags a word tag to each name and presses Check. Success: Window North and Bed East turn green; the cupboard accepts West or North and the bedside table accepts South or East, with "This thing sits between two directions. We name the nearest one. Sample answer: window north, bed east, cupboard west, bedside table south. Your answer may differ."
- Star Challenge 4 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Make a drawing of your room and locate the direction in which different things have been placed in relation to you standing at the centre of the room. Make the direction arrow for your room." then "Write the names of the things that are placed in the following directions. East ___ West ___ North ___ South ___" Goal chip: "Draw my room". The child drags at least 3 cut-outs onto the plan as in their own room, fills the direction arrow with N, E, S, W, then drags a placed thing into each name box (or "nothing here"). Guess: the child presses Check when done. Success: each thing is in the zone of its box; the strip reads the child's own answer, for example "East: bed. West: cupboard. North: window. South: door. Your answer may differ."
- End screen (confetti once): "Well done!" Remember: "North is up, south is down, east is right and west is left on a picture with a compass." "A direction is always said from a place or a person." "If A is east of B, then B is west of A." Think and talk: "The cupboard is west of the girl. Which direction is the girl from the cupboard?" Button: "Start again".
8. Assets and Language
- Images: photo-style grass; flat drawings of a flagpole, library, canteen, cricket net and water tank; the camp from above; the girl's room in perspective; a wooden floor; eight room cut-outs; four pens; compass card and cross (code). English.

media.teaching_notes: Start from one thing, then follow the arrow named by the word. The compass says N is at the top, so up is north. The slip to watch: reading east and west the wrong way round, as if the left of the picture were east.

The top of the picture is north. Read the compass first. N is at the top, S at the bottom, E on the right and W on the left. A thing drawn above another thing is north of it. Below is south. To the right is east. To the left is west. Try it on a playground: a swing at the top left, a slide at the top right, a sandpit at the bottom left and a seesaw at the bottom right. The slide is to the right of the swing, so the slide is east of the swing. Always begin from one thing and look in a direction. East of the swing is the slide. West of the seesaw is the sandpit. South of the slide: look below the slide. The seesaw is there. 4. West of the seesaw: look to the left of the seesaw. The sandpit is there. 5. North of the sandpit: look above the sandpit. The swing is there. 6. Check: the swing and the slide are in the top row and the sandpit and the seesaw are in the bottom row, and the top row is north of the bottom row. Answer: The slide is east of the swing, the seesaw is south of the slide, the sandpit is west of the seesaw and the swing is north of the sandpit

content.text:
1. Find the compass. $N$ is at the top, so above is north, below is south, left is west and right is east.
2. Clue $1$: the tent to the west of the road is blue. West is to the left, so colour blue the tent on the left of the road.
3. Clue $2$: the tent closest to the lake is green. Colour green the tent just above the lake.
[Image: Bird Watching: Ans1: solution]
4. Clue $3$: the tent north of the green tent is purple. North is above, so colour purple the tent above the green tent, near the top.
5. Clue $4$: the tent south of the lake is yellow. South is below, so colour yellow the tent below the lake.
6. Check: there are four clues and four tents, and each tent has its own colour: blue, green, purple and yellow.
Answer: Blue: the tent left of the road. Green: the tent just above the lake. Purple: the tent above the green tent. Yellow: the tent below the lake.
[Image: Bird Watching: Ans1: solution (continued)]

media.title: Bus Route Driver

tool_config.idea: Steer a bus along the street map and see that a turn is right or left while a direction is north, east, south or west: a right turn changes north to east, east to south, south to west and west to north, and a left turn changes the direction the other way round.
tool_config.title: Bus Route Driver
tool_config.screen: The street map board on the trip desk, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. The street map of your maths book is the largest thing on screen, seen from above: the PARKING area at the bottom, Hospital Road along the top with the Hospital above it, Park Road down the right side with the Children's Park at the top right, Market Road across the middle between the Basketball Court and the Shopping Centre, and the houses of Lali, Rohan, Ravi, Prem, Raju, Tinku, Jaideep and Golu. Stop 1 (S1) stands at the hospital gate and Stop 2 (S2) beside the Shopping Centre. A yellow school bus stands on the PARKING area facing north. A compass card in the top right corner shows N at the top, E in red on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with progress dots under it. A heading panel under the compass reads The bus is driving: north, with a small arrow that turns with the bus, and a line Last turn: none that changes to right or left after each turn. A road strip lists the names of the roads the bus has driven on, in order. Controls: Forward (one block), Turn right and Turn left (the bus turns on the spot at a junction and leaves a red dotted trail behind it); road name tags Hospital Road, Market Road and Park Road that can be tapped; a tap on a house or a stop selects it; a Trace switch that, when it is on, puts a round orange marker on the gate of the house the student taps instead of the bus, so that the same Forward, Turn right and Turn left buttons steer it along the roads and leave an orange trail; an answer strip for the book's sentences with blank slots and chips (road chips Hospital, Market and Park; direction chips north, east, south and west; turn chips right and left); Check, Hint, Undo (takes back the last move), Retry (returns the bus to its last stop), Reset (returns the bus to the PARKING area and clears the trail), Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: the heading panel, the road strip, a blocks driven counter and a card number out of 7.
feedback: Every turn updates the heading panel with a sentence that names both the turn and the direction, for example: The bus was driving north. A right turn makes it drive east.
Forward moves the bus one block along its road and adds to the red dotted trail. If the bus faces a corner where it cannot go on, a soft amber note says: The road ends here. Turn right or turn left.
A tap on a road name tag checks the road under the bus. A wrong tag shows a soft amber note such as: Look at the name written on the road under the bus.
In Trace mode, a move that leaves the roads is refused with: The marker can move only along the roads. Press Undo to go back to the last junction.

For the questions about houses and stops, a wrong tap shows a clue, for example: East is on the right of the compass. Look across Park Road, to the right of Jaideep's House. The tool never shows the full answer before the last hint.
A traced route is never marked wrong when it stays on the roads and ends at the right place. The tool says Your answer may differ and offers Next.
tool_config.done_when: The bus has been steered with right and left turns, the direction after each turn has been read, the blanks for Stop 1 and Stop 2 are filled correctly, and the five questions on the street map are answered, with a route traced from Ravi's house and from Golu's house.

placement.where: last concept of the topic, after its teaching and worked examples

challenges: Card 1: drive the bus north from the PARKING area to the Hospital Road corner, then press Turn right. Read the heading panel. Which direction is the bus driving after the turn? Answer: east, because a right turn changes north to east.
Card 2: drive east along Hospital Road to the Park Road corner and press Turn right again. Which direction is the bus driving now? Answer: south, because a right turn changes east to south.

Card 3 (practice values): put the bus on a side road facing north and press Turn right four times, reading the heading panel each time. Answer: east, then south, then west, then north. After four right turns the bus faces north again.
Card 4 (practice values): put the bus on a side road facing east and press Turn left, then Turn left again. Answer: north, then west, because a left turn changes east to north and north to west.

Card 5 (practice values): drive the bus north from the PARKING area only as far as the Market Road corner, press Turn right and tap the road name tag of the road the bus is on. Which road, and which direction? Answer: Market Road, driving east, because a right turn changes north to east.

Challenge: 'The bus will start from the parking area. It will go north and then it will take a right turn onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction to reach Stop 1 (S1).' and 'To reach Stop 2 (S2), it will turn ___ (right/left) onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction.' Drive the route with the heading panel hidden, then fill the blanks with the chips. Answer: Hospital, east; then right, Park, south. A right turn changes north to east and a right turn changes east to south.

Challenge: (a) 'Whose houses are situated to the east of Jaideep's house?' (b) 'Mark the route from Ravi's house to the children's park.' (c) 'Which stop is closer to Lali's house?' (d) 'Golu is running late. Trace the route to help him reach the nearest bus stop.' (e) 'In which direction would Prem have to move to reach Stop 2?' Answers: (a) Prem's house and Raju's house. (b) Sample answer: south to the small road, east to the main road, north to Hospital Road, east to Park Road and the Children's Park. (c) Stop 1 (S1). (d) Sample answer: south to the road below, east to Park Road, north to Hospital Road, west to Stop 1. (e) South. Other routes along the roads are right too, and your answer may differ.

hint_ladder.text: Which way is the bus facing now? Look at the heading panel, or at the arrow on the bus. Is the next turn right or left?
Say the direction before the turn. Then ask: after a right turn, which direction comes next? A right turn goes north, east, south, west. A left turn goes north, west, south, east.
If the bus drives north and turns right, it drives east. If it drives east and turns right, it drives south. Use this to fill the blank.
The tool turns the bus for you and shows the new direction in the heading panel. Then it gives you a similar turn to try yourself.

media.instructions_for_student: The student understands that a turn is right or left while a direction is north, east, south or west, and says which direction a bus drives after each turn on a street map.
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Bus Route Driver
B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M2.S7.T7.C24.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity
- Textbook source: Maps and Locations, Zoo Trip and Bus Route: the street map with its red dotted route, the two sentences for Stop 1 and Stop 2, and questions (a) to (e). No numbers (developer only).
C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student says the direction a bus drives after a right or a left turn, names the road it turns onto, and reads a street map to find houses, stops and routes.
- Out of scope: distances on the map, in-between directions.
D. TOOL DESCRIPTION
1. Opening Screen
- A practice map, Orchard Town, seen from above: four grey roads make a square ring, Mill Road (top), Dairy Road (bottom), Well Road (left), Temple Road (right), names written along them; orchard trees and a pond inside. A yellow school bus (top view, about 12 percent of the stage width long) stands at the top right corner facing south, with a round dial above it: "The bus is driving: south". The compass card (N top, E red right, S bottom, W left) is in the top right corner.
- Instruction line: "Drive the bus to the corner. Then turn right."
- The child is invited to press "Go" on the steering pad.
2. Scene and Objects
- Steering pad: three big round buttons at the bottom centre: "Go" (the bus drives straight to the next corner or junction), "Turn left" and "Turn right" (a quarter turn onto the road that begins there). The bus leaves a red dotted trail. Practice map corners: Mill and Well (top left), Mill and Temple (top right), Dairy and Well (bottom left), Dairy and Temple (bottom right); no other road joins the ring.
- The book's street map (Star Challenges), from above, N at the top: Hospital Road along the top with the Hospital above it; Children's Park at the top right; Park Road down the right side; Tinku's House and Golu's House just below Hospital Road; below them a pond block with Jaideep's House; the Basketball Court; Market Road; the Shopping Centre; PARKING at the bottom; Lali's House and Rohan's House top left, Ravi's House left in the middle; Prem's House and Raju's House east of Park Road. Stop 1 (S1) is at the hospital gate, Stop 2 (S2) beside the Shopping Centre, near Park Road.
- Chips for the book's sentences: "Hospital", "Market", "Park"; "north", "east", "south", "west"; "right", "left". One goal chip at the top; a curved-arrow icon is Undo.
3. Main Interaction
- "Go", "Turn left" and "Turn right" steer the bus; a turn works only at a corner or junction, towards a road that exists. After a turn the child taps the name of the road the bus is on, printed on the map.
- In the book's map challenges the child taps chips into blanks, taps houses, stops or a compass letter, or drags a finger along the roads (the line snaps to the roads and is read out, for example "south, east, north, east").
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" and the main button "Check", which becomes "Next" when the goal chip is green.
4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided). Goal line: "Drive the bus to the corner and turn right." Goal chip: "Turn right at the corner". Setup: bus at the top right corner facing south, dial on. The child presses Go: the bus drives down Temple Road to the bottom right corner. Guess: before turning, the child taps a letter on the compass card for the direction the bus will drive after the turn. Result: the bus drives west along Dairy Road; the guessed W turns green with a bounce; then the child taps "Dairy Road". Why line: "The bus was driving south. A right turn makes it drive west." Help: guided, the road under the bus pulses.
- Activity 2 (guided). Goal line: "Turn right again at the next corner." Goal chip: "Turn right again". Setup: the bus at the bottom right corner facing west, dial on. The child presses Go to the bottom left corner. Guess: the child taps a letter. Result: the bus drives north along Well Road; the child taps "Well Road". Why line: "The bus was driving west. A right turn makes it drive north."
- Activity 3 (guided, less help). Goal line: "Now turn left at the corner." Goal chip: "Turn left at the corner". Setup: the bus is carried to the bottom left corner facing east, dial on. The child presses Go to the bottom right corner. Guess: the child taps a letter. Result: the bus drives north along Temple Road; the child taps "Temple Road". Why line: "The bus was driving east. A left turn makes it drive north."
- Activity 4 (independent). Goal line: "The bus drives south. Turn left at the corner." Goal chip: "Turn left, driving south". Setup: the bus at the top left corner facing south on Well Road; dial hidden. The child presses Go to the bottom left corner. Guess: the child taps a letter. Result: the bus drives east along Dairy Road; the child taps "Dairy Road". Why line: "The bus was driving south. A left turn makes it drive east." Help: independent, no dial.
- Star Challenges: see section 7.
5. Mathematical Understanding
- A turn tells which hand you turn towards; a direction tells where you go. The same turn gives different directions, depending on the way the bus drives now.
- A right turn takes north to east, east to south, south to west and west to north; a left turn goes the other way round. The Remember lines of section 7 say it.
6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the letter turns green with a bounce, the dial arrow turns, the strip shows the why line.
- Mistake: taps E after a right turn from south (a right turn always means east) -> red strip, small shake: "A right turn does not always make the bus drive east. Look at which way the bus drives now, then turn to your right." The dial arrow pulses. The direction it already drives -> "A turn changes the direction. Look at the dial."
- Mistake: wrong road name -> "Look at the name written on the road under the bus." Go at a dead end -> "The road ends here. Turn right or turn left."
- Mistake: Challenge 1, Market -> "That is Market Road, across the middle of the map. Stop 1 is at the hospital gate. Read the name of the road near the Hospital."
- Mistake: Challenge 2, a house left of Park Road -> "East is on the right of the compass. Look across Park Road, to the right of Jaideep's House." Stop 2 for Lali -> "Look at where Lali's House is, at the top left. Which stop is nearer to it?" W for Prem -> "Stop 2 is more below Prem's House than to the left. Which of the four directions is it mostly?"
- Mistake: Challenge 3, a line off the roads -> "The line must stay on the roads. Go back to the last junction."
- Hint button, 3 levels: (1) words: "Which way is the bus driving now? Look at the dial. Is the turn right or left?"; (2) visual: two small hands appear on the bus with their directions written (driving south: right hand "west", left hand "east"); (3) almost the answer: "The bus is driving south. Its right hand points west. A right turn makes it drive west." For map questions: the place you look from pulses, an arrow runs in the direction asked, then the answer pulses.
7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "The bus will start from the parking area. It will go north and then it will take a right turn onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction to reach Stop 1 (S1)." and "To reach Stop 2 (S2), it will turn ___ (right/left) onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction." Goal chip: "Fill the blanks". Setup: the book's street map; the bus on the PARKING area facing north; chips under the sentences. Guess: the child taps chips into the five blanks and presses Check; nothing is said before Check. Success: the bus drives the child's route with the dial on: north, a right turn onto Hospital Road driving east to Stop 1, on to Park Road, a right turn onto Park Road driving south to Stop 2. Blanks: Hospital, east; right, Park, south. Why line: "The bus was driving north and turned right onto Hospital Road. A right turn makes it drive east. Then it turned right onto Park Road: east to south." A wrong answer makes the bus drive the wrong road and stop.
- Star Challenge 2 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Whose houses are situated to the east of Jaideep's house? ___" then "Which stop is closer to Lali's house? ___" then "In which direction would Prem have to move to reach Stop 2?" Goal chip: "3 questions on the map". Guess: the child taps houses, a stop and a compass letter, then presses Check for each. Success: Prem's House and Raju's House glow; Stop 1 is chosen; S glows. Why lines: "Prem's House and Raju's House are on the right of Park Road, on the east side." "No distances are printed, so we judge from the picture: Stop 1 is near the top, close to Lali's House." "Stop 2 is below Prem's House, so Prem moves south."
- Star Challenge 3 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Mark the route from Ravi's house to the children's park." then "Golu is running late. Trace the route to help him reach the nearest bus stop." Goal chip: "Trace 2 routes". Guess: the child drags a finger from the house gate along the roads and presses Check. Success: a route on the roads that ends at the Children's Park gate, and a route from Golu's House that ends at Stop 1, turn green and are read in words. Sample routes: Ravi's house south, east to the main road, north to Hospital Road, east to Park Road and the park; Golu's house south, east to Park Road, north to Hospital Road, west to Stop 1. "Your answer may differ: other routes along the roads are right too."
- End screen (confetti once): "Well done!" Remember: "A right turn takes north to east, east to south, south to west and west to north." "A left turn goes the other way round: north to west, west to south, south to east and east to north." "A turn is right or left. A direction is north, east, south or west." Think and talk: "Can a right turn make a bus drive west? Which way was the bus driving before the turn?" Button: "Start again".
8. Assets and Language
- Images: flat top-view Orchard Town; a yellow school bus (top-view cut-out); the book's street map redrawn from above (roads, Hospital, park, court, shopping centre, parking, eight houses with labels, stop signs S1 and S2); the red dotted route (code); the compass card. English.

content.text:
1. Predict first: a bus is driving north and takes a right turn. Which direction is it driving now: east, south or west?
2. East. A turn says which hand you turn towards. A direction says where you are going. They are two different things.
3. Face north and hold out your arms. Your right hand points east and your left hand points west. A right turn takes you towards your right hand.
4. A right turn changes north to east, east to south, south to west and west to north.
5. A left turn changes the direction the other way round: north to west, west to south, south to east and east to north.
6. A right turn does not always make a bus drive east. A bus that is driving east and turns right drives south.
7. To read a route, say two things at every turn: right or left, and the direction after the turn.
8. Rule: a right turn takes the direction through north, east, south, west in that order. A left turn takes it through north, west, south, east.

content.text:
Worked example: A cycle drives north along a road and turns left at a junction. Which direction is it driving after the turn? At the next junction it turns left again. Which direction is it driving now?
1. The cycle drives north. Face north: your left hand points west and your right hand points east.
2. A left turn is a turn towards the left hand. The left hand points west, so after the first turn the cycle drives west.
3. Now the cycle drives west. Face west: your left hand points south.
4. The second left turn is towards south, so the cycle now drives south.
5. Check with the rule: a left turn takes north to west, and west to south.
6. The two left turns together made the cycle drive the opposite way to the way it started: it started north and now drives south.
Answer: After the first left turn the cycle drives west. After the second left turn it drives south

media.title: Metro Route Planner

tool_config.idea: Read the metro map as a network: ride a coloured line, change lines only at a capsule that shows both colours, and read the counter of stations between two stations, counting every circle and capsule between the two ends but not the ends.
tool_config.title: Metro Route Planner
tool_config.screen: A station information board on the trip desk, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. The Delhi metro map of your maths book is the largest thing on screen: eight coloured lines (Red, Yellow, Blue, Airport Express, Green, Violet, Pink and Magenta), circles for stations, capsules for interchanges, and the station names that are printed on the map, such as Qutb Minar, Hauz Khas, INA, Rajiv Chowk, Supreme Court, Mayur Vihar and Botanical Garden. A key panel beside the map lists the 10 symbols of the key: the 8 coloured lines, 9 Metro Station (a plain circle) and 10 Interchange Line (a capsule with two coloured dots). A route card at the right lists the lines used and the stations where the lines change. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with progress dots under it. Controls: tap a start station and an end station; tap a line colour in the key panel to ride along that line, and a thick highlight in that colour grows along the line; tap a capsule to change line; a Mark switch that puts an orange ring on a tapped station; a Save route button that keeps up to 3 routes on the route card; answer cards that click into an answer strip; Undo (takes back the last ride), Clear route, Check, Hint, Retry (clears the route of this question), Reset (clears the whole board), Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: a counter stations between that updates with every circle or capsule passed, not counting the two ends, a changes count and the list of change stations on the route card, and a card number out of 7.
feedback: Each ride highlights the part of the line in its own colour and the counter updates at once, for example: Between Mayur Vihar and Botanical Garden there are 5 stations, not counting the two ends.
A tap on a capsule shows its two colours and offers the change, for example: Hauz Khas shows yellow and magenta, so you can change from the Yellow Line to the Magenta Line here.
A tap on a crossing without a capsule gives a soft amber note: You can change lines only where the capsule shows both colours. Here the lines only cross.
A route that stops before the end station says where it stopped, for example: This route stops at Hauz Khas. Keep riding until you reach Supreme Court.
A count that includes the two ends shows a clue, for example: Do not count the first and the last station. Count only the circles between them.
Open questions, the routes and the best way, are never marked wrong when every change is at a capsule that shows both colours: the tool says Your answer may differ and offers Next.
tool_config.done_when: The key symbols are matched, the counter has been read on two lines, the crossing without a capsule has been tested, the two stations are marked, at least two routes are traced from Qutb Minar to Supreme Court with their stations between counted, and the questions about Lali's suggestion, the fewest stations and the best way are answered.

placement.where: last concept of the topic, after its teaching and worked examples

challenges: Card 1: match the key. Drag the names to the symbols: a plain circle and a capsule with two coloured dots. Answer: the plain circle is a Metro Station and the capsule with two coloured dots is an Interchange Line.
Card 2 (practice values): ride the Blue Line from Mayur Vihar to Botanical Garden and read the counter. Answer: 5 stations between, not counting Mayur Vihar and Botanical Garden.
Card 3 (practice values): ride the Pink Line from INA to Mayur Vihar and read the counter. Answer: 5 stations between. The capsule where the Pink Line meets the Violet Line counts as one of the 5.

Card 4: tap the place where the Airport Express Line crosses the Magenta Line. Can you change lines there? Answer: no. There is no capsule, so the lines only cross. You can change lines only at a capsule that shows both colours.
Card 5 (practice values): ride the Yellow Line from Hauz Khas to Central Secretariat. The capsule at INA counts as one station. How many stations are between? Answer: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 stations between.

Challenge: 'What do the different coloured lines represent?' and 'Mark the Qutb Minar station on the Yellow Line and the Supreme Court station on the Blue Line.' Build the first answer from the cards and mark the two stations with rings. Answer: each coloured line is a different metro route; Qutb Minar is the labelled circle on the lower part of the Yellow Line, next to Saket, and Supreme Court is the labelled circle on the Blue Line, the third station after Rajiv Chowk.

Challenge: (a) 'Look at the metro map and trace different routes from the Qutb Minar metro station to the Supreme Court metro station.' (b) 'Lali says, "We can take the Yellow Line and change the metro at Hauz Khas to take the Magenta Line." If the children follow Lali's suggestion, at which station(s) do they need to change the metro line again to reach the Supreme Court metro station?' (c) 'Which route has the least number of stations between Qutb Minar and Supreme Court?' (d) 'Which metro route(s), do you think, is/are the best way to reach the zoo from Qutb Minar?' Answers: (a) Sample answer: Route A, the Yellow Line to Rajiv Chowk and then the Blue Line, 14 stations between and 1 change; Route B, the Yellow Line to INA, the Pink Line to Mayur Vihar and then the Blue Line, 15 stations between and 2 changes; Route C, the Yellow Line to Hauz Khas, the Magenta Line to Botanical Garden and then the Blue Line, 25 stations between and 2 changes. (b) Botanical Garden, where the Magenta Line meets the Blue Line. (c) Route A, with 14 stations between. (d) Sample answer: Route A, because it has the fewest stations (14) and only one change, at Rajiv Chowk. Your answer may differ.

hint_ladder.text: Which line are you on? Look at the colour of the highlight and at the route card.
Where does your line meet the next line? A capsule shows two coloured dots. You can change lines only at a capsule that shows both colours.
Count the circles between the two ends, not the ends. A capsule counts as one station. Watch the counter as you ride.
The tool highlights the route for you and reads the count of stations between. Then it gives you a similar route to try yourself.

media.instructions_for_student: The student reads a metro map by following a coloured line, changing lines only at a capsule, and counting the stations between two stations without counting the two ends.
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Metro Route Planner
B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M2.S10.T10.C41.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity
- Textbook source: Maps and Locations, Delhi Metro Train Stations: the metro map with its key of 10 symbols and the six questions on it. Counts used (circles and capsules between the two ends): Route A 14, Route B 15, Route C 25 (developer only).
C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student follows a coloured metro line, changes lines only at a capsule, and counts the stations between two stations without counting the two ends.
- Out of scope: fares, timetables, distances between stations.
D. TOOL DESCRIPTION
1. Opening Screen
- The Delhi metro map, redrawn from the book in clean lines, fills the stage: eight coloured lines (Red, Yellow, Blue, Airport Express in orange, Green, Violet, Pink, Magenta), a white circle at every station, a capsule with two coloured dots at every interchange, a pale blue river band and the station names. The key with its 10 symbols is at the bottom right. Two pills at the top left read "Stations between: 0" and "Changes: 0".
- Instruction line: "Find the capsule at Kashmeri Gate. Which two lines meet there?"
- The child is invited to tap two colours in the key, then the capsule.
2. Scene and Objects
- The map is code-drawn from the book's map with the same stations on each line. Printed names are those of the book's map, including Qutb Minar, Saket, Hauz Khas, INA, Rajiv Chowk, Supreme Court, Kashmeri Gate, Kalkaji Mandir, Botanical Garden and Mundka.
- Key: symbols 1 to 8 are the lines; 9 is a circle, "Metro Station"; 10 is a capsule with two coloured dots, "Interchange Line".
- A ride glows along the line in its colour, with an orange ring on the start and a green ring on the end. Small icons on the stage: Undo (curved arrow) and a star that saves a finished route (up to three, shown as chips "Route A", "Route B", "Route C"). One goal chip at the top.
3. Main Interaction
- Tap a start station, then a station farther along the same line: the part between glows and the counter shows the stations between. A station on another line gives "These two stations are on different lines. Ride to a capsule that shows both colours first."
- To change line, tap the capsule: its two dots become two colour buttons; tap a colour to ride on, then tap the next station. Lines that only cross give no change.
- Counting rule: every circle and capsule strictly between the first and the last station counts once; the two ends never count; a capsule where you change counts as one.
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" and the main button "Check", which becomes "Next" when the goal chip is green. Reset clears the board.
4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided). Goal line: "Find the capsule at Kashmeri Gate. Which two lines meet there?" Goal chip: "Two lines meet". Guess: before tapping the capsule, the child taps two colours in the key. Result: the capsule grows and shows a yellow dot and a red dot; the chips Yellow and Red turn green. Why line: "Kashmeri Gate has a yellow dot and a red dot, so the Yellow Line and the Red Line meet here. You can change lines here." Help: guided, the capsule and its key symbol pulse.
- Activity 2 (guided). Goal line: "Ride the Blue Line from Rajouri Garden to Kriti Nagar. How many stations are between?" Goal chip: "Stations between". Setup: Rajouri Garden (blue and pink capsule) is "start", Kriti Nagar (blue and green capsule) is "end". Guess: before riding, the child taps "2", "3" or "4". Result: the Blue Line glows, bubbles "1" and "2" pop over the two circles, the counter shows 2. Why line: "Between Rajouri Garden and Kriti Nagar there are 2 stations, not counting the two ends." Help: guided, bubbles on every station passed.
- Activity 3 (guided, less help). Goal line: "Ride the Blue Line from Janakpuri West to Kriti Nagar. Count the stations between." Goal chip: "Count with a capsule". Setup: Janakpuri West (a blue and magenta capsule) to Kriti Nagar; the Rajouri Garden capsule lies between. Guess: the child taps "6", "7" or "8". Result: the counter runs 1 to 4 over four circles, 5 at the Rajouri Garden capsule, 6 and 7 over two circles. Why line: "4 circles, then the capsule at Rajouri Garden counts as 1, then 2 circles: 4 + 1 + 2 = 7 stations between, not counting Janakpuri West and Kriti Nagar." Help: bubbles only on the capsule.
- Activity 4 (independent). Goal line: "Can you change lines where the Airport Express Line crosses the Magenta Line? Tap the crossing." Goal chip: "Cross or change?". Guess: the child taps "Yes" or "No", then the crossing near Delhi Aerocity. Result: the crossing shows no capsule; "No" turns green. Why line: "No. There is no capsule here, so the two lines only cross. You can change lines only at a capsule that shows both colours." Help: independent.
- Star Challenges: see section 7.
5. Mathematical Understanding
- A coloured line is one route, a circle is one station, a capsule with two dots is a station where two lines meet. The line changes only at a capsule. Routes are compared by their stations between.
- The rules to say at the end are the Remember lines of section 7.
6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the ring, card or chip turns green with a gentle bounce, the glow stays, the strip shows the why line.
- Mistake: two lines that are not the dots of the capsule -> red strip, small shake: "Look at the two dots in the capsule. What are their colours?" The capsule pulses.
- Mistake: counts the ends (taps 4 in Activity 2, or 8 in Activity 3) -> "Do not count the first and the last station. Count only the circles between them." The two ends pulse. Leaves out the capsule (taps 6 in Activity 3) -> "A capsule is a station too. Count it as one." The capsule pulses.
- Mistake: Yes in Activity 4 -> "A crossing is not a change. Look for a capsule with two dots."
- Mistake: a route that stops early -> "This route stops at Hauz Khas. Keep riding until you reach Supreme Court." Another card for the fewest stations -> "Count again: which route has the smallest number on the counter?"
- Hint button, 3 levels: (1) words: "Which line are you on? Look at the colour of the glow."; (2) visual: the capsules on your line that show a second colour pulse and the circles show number bubbles; (3) almost the answer: "Count the circles between the two ends, not the ends. A capsule counts as one station." and the tool rides the first leg for you.
7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "What do the different coloured lines represent?" then "Mark the Qutb Minar station on the Yellow Line and the Supreme Court station on the Blue Line." Goal chip: "Lines and stations". A tap on a station puts an orange ring on it (two at most). Three answer cards: "Each coloured line is a different metro route.", "Each colour tells how many people travel.", "Each colour is a different station." Guess: the child taps a card, rings the two stations and presses Check. Success: the first card and both rings turn green. Why line: "Each coloured line is a different metro route. Qutb Minar is on the Yellow Line next to Saket. Supreme Court is on the Blue Line, the third station after Rajiv Chowk."
- Star Challenge 2 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Look at the metro map and trace different routes from the Qutb Minar metro station to the Supreme Court metro station." Goal chip: "2 different routes". The child rides from Qutb Minar and saves each finished route with the star. Guess: the child saves at least two routes and presses Check. Success: every saved route ends at Supreme Court and changes only at capsules; the strip reads each one. Route A, Yellow Line to Rajiv Chowk then the Blue Line: 14 stations between, 1 change. Route B, Yellow Line to INA, Pink Line to Mayur Vihar, Blue Line: 15 stations between, 2 changes. Route C, Yellow Line to Hauz Khas, Magenta Line to Botanical Garden, Blue Line: 25 between, 2 changes. Any other valid route is read the same way, with "Your answer may differ."
- Star Challenge 3 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Lali says, "We can take the Yellow Line and change the metro at Hauz Khas to take the Magenta Line." If the children follow Lali's suggestion, at which station(s) do they need to change the metro line again to reach the Supreme Court metro station?" Goal chip: "Where to change again". Setup: the ride is at Hauz Khas on the Magenta Line. Guess: the child taps the capsule where they would change again and presses Check. Success: Botanical Garden turns green. Why line: "The Magenta Line meets the Blue Line at Botanical Garden, which has a magenta dot and a blue dot. They change there and ride the Blue Line to Supreme Court." Kalkaji Mandir -> "The Violet Line does not go to Supreme Court. Look for the capsule where the Magenta Line meets the Blue Line." Janakpuri West -> "That works, but it is a much longer way. Is there a shorter one?"
- Star Challenge 4 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Which route has the least number of stations between Qutb Minar and Supreme Court?" then "Which metro route(s), do you think, is/are the best way to reach the zoo from Qutb Minar? ___" Goal chip: "Fewest stations". Setup: route cards "Route A", "Route B", "Route C". Guess: the child taps the card they think has the fewest stations between; then each card rides and the counter runs to 14, 15 and 25. Success: Route A turns green. Why line: "Route A has 14 stations between. 14 is less than 15, and 15 is less than 25." For the best way the child taps a card and a reason chip ("It has the fewest stations." "It has the fewest changes."); any card with a reason turns green: "Sample answer: Route A, because it has the fewest stations (14) and only one change, at Rajiv Chowk. Your answer may differ."
- End screen (confetti once): "Well done!" Remember: "A coloured line is one metro route." "Change lines only at a capsule that shows both colours." "Count the stations between two stations, and do not count the two ends." Think and talk: "Why do we not count the first station and the last station when we count the stations between?" Button: "Start again".
8. Assets and Language
- Images: the metro map redrawn in code from the book (coloured lines, circles, two-dot capsules, a pale blue river band, names); the key; route chips; orange and green rings. English.

content.text:

hold_back: Route A: the Yellow Line to Rajiv Chowk, then the Blue Line. It has 14 stations between, fewer than Route B (15) and Route C (25).

media.teaching_notes: 1. Count the stations between Qutb Minar and Supreme Court on each route. A capsule where we change counts as one station. Do not count Qutb Minar or Supreme Court. 2. Route A: count the circles on the Yellow Line from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas (2), Hauz Khas (1), then 2 to INA, INA (1), 3 to Central Secretariat, Central Secretariat (1), 1 to Rajiv Chowk, Rajiv Chowk (1), then 2 on the Blue Line to Supreme Court. 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 14. 3. Route B: 5 stations from Qutb Minar to INA, INA (1), 5 on the Pink Line to Mayur Vihar, Mayur Vihar (1), 1 to Yamuna Bank, Yamuna Bank (1), 1 to Supreme Court. 5 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 15. 4. Route C: 3 stations from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas, 4 on the Magenta Line to Kalkaji Mandir, Kalkaji Mandir (1), 7 to Botanical Garden, Botanical Garden (1), 5 on the Blue Line to Mayur Vihar, Mayur Vihar (1), 1 to Yamuna Bank, Yamuna Bank (1), 1 to Supreme Court. 3 + 4 + 1 + 7 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 25. 5. 14 is less than 15, and 15 is less than 25, so Route A has the fewest stations between. 6. Check: Route A changes at Rajiv Chowk, the capsule where the Yellow Line meets the Blue Line, so it stays on the Yellow Line the longest. 5. Check each change: Rajiv Chowk, $INA$, Mayur Vihar, Hauz Khas and Botanical Garden are all capsules that show the colours of both lines.
6. Your answer may differ: other routes on the map are right too.
Answer: Sample answer: $A$, Yellow to Rajiv Chowk, then Blue. $B$, Yellow to $INA$, Pink to Mayur Vihar, then Blue. $C$, Yellow to Hauz Khas, Magenta to Botanical Garden, then Blue.

content.text:
1. Lali's plan: ride the Yellow Line from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas and change there to the Magenta Line.

[Image: Metro Routes: Ans2: solution]
3. The Magenta Line meets the Blue Line at the capsule Botanical Garden, which has a magenta dot and a blue dot. They change there to the Blue Line.
4. Ride the Blue Line to Supreme Court. So the children change again at Botanical Garden.

6. Check: Botanical Garden is a capsule that shows the colours of both lines, Magenta and Blue.
Answer: Botanical Garden, where the Magenta Line meets the Blue Line. The other way, at Janakpuri West, is much longer.

content.text:
1. Count the stations between Qutb Minar and Supreme Court on each route. A capsule where we change counts as one station. Do not count Qutb Minar or Supreme Court.
2. Route $A$: count the circles on the Yellow Line from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas $(2)$, Hauz Khas $(1)$, then $2$ to $INA$, $INA (1)$, $3$ to Central Secretariat, Central Secretariat $(1)$, $1$ to Rajiv Chowk, Rajiv Chowk $(1)$, then $2$ on the Blue Line to Supreme Court. $2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 14$.
[Image: Metro Routes: Ans3: solution]
3. Route $B$: $5$ stations from Qutb Minar to $INA$, $INA (1)$, $5$ on the Pink Line to Mayur Vihar, Mayur Vihar $(1)$, $1$ to Yamuna Bank, Yamuna Bank $(1)$, $1$ to Supreme Court. $5 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 15$.
4. Route $C$: $3$ stations from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas, $4$ on the Magenta Line to Kalkaji Mandir, Kalkaji Mandir $(1)$, $7$ to Botanical Garden, Botanical Garden $(1)$, $5$ on the Blue Line to Mayur Vihar, Mayur Vihar $(1)$, $1$ to Yamuna Bank, Yamuna Bank $(1)$, $1$ to Supreme Court. $3 + 4 + 1 + 7 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 25$.
5. $14$ is less than $15$, and $15$ is less than $25$, so Route $A$ has the fewest stations between.
6. Check: Route A changes at Rajiv Chowk, the capsule where the Yellow Line meets the Blue Line, so it stays on the Yellow Line the longest.
Answer: Route $A$: the Yellow Line to Rajiv Chowk, then the Blue Line. It has $14$ stations between, fewer than Route $B (15)$ and Route $C (25)$.
