content.text:
Worked example: Make a map of a library corner seen from above: 2 shelves on the west wall, 1 table with 4 chairs in the middle, and the door on the south wall. Make a key, and hide a bookmark with a red dot.
1. Draw the floor of the corner from above as a large rectangle. With N at the top, the west wall is the left side and the south wall is the bottom side.
2. Draw 2 long rectangles along the west wall, one for each shelf. A long rectangle is the symbol for a shelf.
3. Draw 1 square in the middle for the table and 4 small squares around it for the 4 chairs.
4. Draw a gap in the south wall for the door.
5. Hide the bookmark under the table and mark it with a red dot.
6. Make the key. A long rectangle means shelf. A square with 4 small squares around it means table and chairs. A gap in the wall means door. A red dot means the hidden bookmark.
7. Read the map to find the bookmark: start at the door on the south wall, walk north to the table, and look under it.
8. Check: every symbol on the map is in the key, and there is 1 red dot.
Answer: The map has 2 shelves, a table with 4 chairs and a door, a key that explains each symbol, and a red dot under the table. From the door, walk north to the table to find the bookmark

content.text:
1. Choose the places to show. In this sample school there is a gate in the west wall, a road along the west side, a building on the east side, a tree and a bench near the middle, and a garden near the south wall on the west side.
2. Draw the school from above with $N$ at the top, and draw one symbol for each kind of place. For example a rectangle with two squares for the building, a long rectangle for the bench, a cloud shape for the tree.
[Image: Let us do: Ans1: solution]
3. Make the key: a small box that shows each symbol with its name, gate, road, building, tree, seat or bench, garden, and the red dot for a hidden object.
4. Hide $3$ objects: one beside the bench, one beside the tree and one in the garden. Mark each place with a red dot.
5. Write a challenge for a friend: start at the gate and walk east to the tree. The hidden object is a little south of the tree.
6. Check: every symbol on the map is in the key, there are $3$ red dots, and the clue uses only north, east, south and west.
7. Your map will be different: use your own school, your own symbols and your own clue.
Answer: Sample answer: a map with a key and $3$ red dots. Clue: start at the gate, walk east to the tree. The object is a little south of it. Your map will be different.

media.title: Ant Path

tool_config.idea: Build a path on a grid one square at a time and read it as legs, each with a distance in cm and a direction, then compare routes to the same food by their lengths: the shortest route goes only towards the food.
tool_config.title: Ant Path
tool_config.screen: The ant grid board on the trip desk, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. A friendly wooden desk holds one large board: a grid of 11 by 11 squares, each square 1 cm, as in your maths book. The grid is the largest thing on screen. A compass card sits in the top left corner of the grid with N at the top, E in red on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left, and the label 1 cm with a small double arrow sits in the top right corner. A small ant stands on a grid point near the middle. In the book challenges the four foods sit where your maths book puts them: a plate of laddoos 2 squares to the right of the ant, a pile of sugar 3 squares above it, a slice of bread 3 squares to the left and 2 squares below it, and an apple 3 squares to the right and 3 squares below it. In the practice cards the foods are replaced by a leaf, a seed and a berry that the tool places (practice values). In the book challenges the red dashed route drawn in your maths book is shown as a faint guide to follow. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with progress dots under it. Controls: four large arrow buttons N, E, S and W on the right of the board, and each one moves the ant 1 cm along the grid line and draws a red dashed trail with small arrowheads behind it; Undo takes back the last cm; Clear trail puts the ant back on its start and removes the trail; Save route keeps the trail as a named route for comparing; Compare routes shows two saved routes side by side; a legs card with a number box and a direction chip (north, east, south or west) for each leg, with Add leg and Remove leg, where the answer is written; Check, Hint, Retry (clears the trail and the legs card of this step), Reset (puts the ant back and empties the saved routes), Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: the legs list that the tool writes as the ant moves (for example 3 cm east, then 3 cm south), a length counter in cm (for example Length: 6 cm), the direction of the ant's last move, and, in Compare routes, the two lengths and a line such as Route B is 2 cm longer.
feedback: Every tap moves the ant 1 cm and adds to the trail. The legs list joins moves in the same direction into one leg, for example: 3 cm east, then 3 cm south.
The length counter adds the cm of all the legs, for example 3 + 3 = 6, and shows it as Length: 6 cm.
If the ant is not on the food yet, a soft amber note says how far is left and which way, for example: The sugar is 1 cm more towards the north.

A wrong number or direction on the legs card shows a soft amber note that points at the first thing to look at, for example: Count the squares on this leg again. Up is north. The tool shows the expected leg only after the second try.

In Compare routes the tool writes the two lengths and why they differ, for example: Route A is 7 cm and Route B is 9 cm. Route B is 2 cm longer because it has a step 1 cm towards the west, away from the berry.

The other routes to the apple are open answers and are never marked wrong: the tool checks that each route ends on the apple, reads its length, says whether it is a shortest route, and says: Your answer may differ.
tool_config.done_when: The student has moved the ant to the practice foods and read their legs and lengths, compared two routes to one berry, written the legs for the laddoos, the sugar, the bread and the apple, and named the shortest routes to the apple.

placement.where: last concept of the topic, after its teaching and worked examples

challenges: Card 1 (practice values): a leaf lies 4 cm to the west of the ant. Move the ant to the leaf with the arrow buttons. What does the legs list say, and how long is the path? Answer: 4 cm west, and the length is 4 cm, because 4 squares of 1 cm each are 4 cm.

Card 2 (practice values): a berry lies 2 cm to the east and 4 cm to the north of the ant. Move the ant to the berry and read the legs list and the length. Answer: 2 cm east, then 4 cm north, and the length is 2 + 4 = 6 cm.

Card 3 (practice values): a berry lies 4 cm to the east and 3 cm to the north. Build Route A, 4 cm east then 3 cm north, and save it. Build Route B, 5 cm east, 3 cm north, then 1 cm west, and save it. Press Compare routes. Answer: Route A is 4 + 3 = 7 cm and Route B is 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 cm, so Route A is 2 cm shorter. Route B has a step 1 cm the wrong way.

Card 4 (practice values): the berry is still 4 cm east and 3 cm north. Build a route with more turns: 2 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm east, then 2 cm north. Is it shorter than Route A, longer, or the same? Answer: the same. Its length is 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 7 cm. It has three turns but it never goes the wrong way, so it is a shortest route too.

Challenge: 'To get to the laddoos, the ant has to crawl how far, and towards which direction? Each square of the grid is 1 cm.' Then: 'To get to the sugar, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction.' Then: 'To get to the bread, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction; then ___ cm in the ___ direction.' Move the ant with the arrow buttons, then fill the legs card. Answers: the laddoos: 2 cm towards the east. The sugar: 3 cm in the north direction. The bread: 3 cm in the west direction; then 2 cm in the south direction (5 cm in all).

Challenge: 'To get to the apple, the ant needs to crawl ___ cm towards ___, and then ___ cm towards ___, and finally ___ cm towards ___.' Then: 'Identify other routes to reach the point where apple is located. Which one is the shortest?' Answers: the apple: 5 cm towards south, 3 cm towards east, and finally 2 cm towards north, which is 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm in all. Sample answer for the other routes: 3 cm east then 3 cm south (6 cm); 3 cm south then 3 cm east (6 cm); 1 cm south, 3 cm east, then 2 cm south (6 cm). The shortest routes are 6 cm, and the route in your maths book is 10 cm. Your routes may differ.

hint_ladder.text: Which food is the ant going to? Look at where it is on the grid: above, below, to the left or to the right of the ant, and about how many squares away.
Count the squares along one straight grid line. Each square is 1 cm. When the route has to turn, a new leg starts. Say the direction of each leg with the compass.
For a berry 2 cm east and 4 cm north: tap E 2 times, then N 4 times. The legs list says 2 cm east, then 4 cm north, and the length is 2 + 4 = 6 cm.
The tool moves the ant 2 cm to the east for you and writes the first leg on the legs card. Now tap N to start the second leg.

student_does: Look at the small practice grid from the video, with the ant and a berry. Tap E two times to move the ant 2 cm towards the east, the first leg of the way to the berry, and read the legs list.
Use the arrow buttons to move the ant to the practice foods, read the legs list and the length counter each time, and save two routes to one berry to compare their lengths.

The book's own questions on the grid of your maths book: how far, and in which direction, the ant crawls to the laddoos, to the sugar, to the bread and to the apple, and the other routes to the apple with the shortest one.

media.instructions_for_student: The student writes a path on a grid as legs of distance in cm and direction, and sees that the shortest route goes only towards the place and not by fewest turns.
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Ant Path
B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M3.S15.T15.C60.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity
- Textbook source: Maps and Locations, Anthill in the Zoo: a grid of 11 by 11 squares of 1 cm; the ant, laddoos 2 cm east, sugar 3 cm north, bread 3 cm west then 2 cm south, apple 5 cm south, 3 cm east, 2 cm north (10 cm), and the question on other routes (developer only). Practice values added here: honey 5 cm east; crumb 4 cm north then 4 cm west; jam 5 cm east and 3 cm north.
C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student writes a path on a grid as legs of distance in cm and direction, and sees that the shortest route to a place goes only towards it.
- Out of scope: other units of length, diagonal paths, positions written as pairs of numbers (the next tool).
D. TOOL DESCRIPTION
1. Opening Screen
- A flat grid of 11 by 11 squares fills the stage, each square 1 cm, grey lines on pale paper. A small brown ant stands on the grid point 5 lines from the left edge and 5 lines from the top edge, the anthill. The compass card is in the top left corner and the label "1 cm" with a small double arrow in the top right corner. A honey jar (photo-style cut-out) stands 5 squares to the right of the ant.
- Instruction line: "How far is the honey from the ant? Make a guess."
- The child is invited to tap a number chip.
2. Scene and Objects
- The ant moves only along grid lines, one square (1 cm) at a time, leaving a red dashed trail with arrowheads. The compass card is the steering pad: tap its N, E, S or W arrow to move the ant 1 cm that way; the ant can also be dragged along a line, snapping to grid points.
- Legs strip under the grid: the tool writes the path as it grows, for example "4 cm north, then 4 cm west", with a counter "Length: 8 cm". In the Star Challenges it is the child's answer sentence.
- Star Challenge places, as in the book: laddoos 2 squares right of the ant, sugar 3 above, bread 3 left and 2 below, a red apple 3 right and 3 below, with the book's red dashed routes drawn faintly. In the activities the foods are a honey jar, a cake slice and a jam jar.
- Answer blanks: a number blank opens a ring of the numbers 1 to 10; a direction blank opens four chips "north", "east", "south", "west". One goal chip at the top; a curved-arrow icon is Undo; a star icon saves a finished route (up to 3).
3. Main Interaction
- One tap on a compass arrow is one square; the ant never leaves the grid. Moves in the same direction join into one leg; a change of direction starts a new leg.
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" and the main button "Check", which becomes "Next" when the goal chip is green. Reset puts the ant on the anthill and clears the trail and saved routes.
4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided). Goal line: "Move the ant to the honey. Count the squares." Goal chip: "Reach the honey". Setup: honey 5 squares east of the ant; legs strip and length counter on; a number bubble pops over each square crossed. Guess: before moving, the child taps "4", "5" or "6" for the number of cm. Result: after five taps on E the ant stands on the honey and the guessed 5 turns green. Why line: "5 squares of 1 cm each are 5 cm. The honey is 5 cm towards the east." Help: guided, bubbles and labels.
- Activity 2 (guided, less help). Goal line: "Move the ant to the cake crumb. It is not in a straight line." Goal chip: "Reach the crumb". Setup: the cake slice is 4 squares north and 4 squares west of the ant; legs strip and counter on, no bubbles. Guess: before moving, the child taps the first direction to go, "north" or "west". Result: either order reaches the crumb; the strip writes "4 cm north, then 4 cm west". Why line: "Two legs: 4 cm north and 4 cm west. Length: 4 + 4 = 8 cm."
- Activity 3 (independent). Goal line: "Make two different routes to the jam. Which is shorter?" Goal chip: "Compare 2 routes". Setup: the jam jar is 5 squares east and 3 squares north of the ant. Guess: before building, the child taps "Route X is shorter", "Route Y is shorter" or "Same". The child builds and saves Route X, 5 cm east then 3 cm north, and Route Y, 2 cm south, 5 cm east, then 5 cm north. Result: both lengths appear side by side, Route X 5 + 3 = 8 cm and Route Y 2 + 5 + 5 = 12 cm, with "Route Y is 4 cm longer." Why line: "Route Y goes 2 cm south, away from the jam, and then needs 2 cm more to come back: 3 + 2 = 5 cm north." Any route that ends on the jam is read the same way. Help: independent.
- Activity 4 (independent). Goal line: "Is a route with more turns longer? Build this route to the jam." Goal chip: "Count cm, not turns". The child builds 2 cm east, 1 cm north, 3 cm east, then 2 cm north. Guess: before building, the child taps "longer than 8 cm", "8 cm" or "shorter than 8 cm". Result: the route ends on the jam; the strip writes 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 = 8 cm and "3 turns, and still 8 cm." Why line: "It never goes the wrong way, so it is as short as the route with one turn. Count the cm, not the turns." Help: independent.
- Star Challenges: see section 7.
5. Mathematical Understanding
- Each square is 1 cm, so counting squares along a line gives the distance and the compass the direction. A path with a turn is a list of legs; its length is their sum. A step the wrong way adds length because it must be walked back, so the shortest routes go only towards the place; the number of turns does not decide the length.
- The rules to say at the end are the Remember lines of section 7.
6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the guess chip or food turns green with a gentle bounce, the ant hops, the strip shows the why line.
- Mistake: the ant is not on the food -> red strip, small shake: "The honey is 1 cm more towards the east." The next square pulses.
- Mistake: counts grid lines instead of squares (says 6 for 5 squares) -> "Count the squares, not the lines. The ant stands on a line." Wrong direction (south for up) -> "Look at the compass. N is at the top, so up is north."
- Mistake: one leg for a food that needs two -> "The food is not in a straight line. How many legs does the route need?" Activity 3, "same" or "Route X is longer" -> "Add the legs of each route. Route X: 5 + 3. Route Y: 2 + 5 + 5." Activity 4, more turns is longer -> "Add the cm of each leg, not the turns: 2 + 1 + 3 + 2."
- Mistake: Challenge 2, the 10 cm route as the shortest -> "This route goes 2 cm north, away from the apple. Is there a route that goes only east and south?"
- Hint button, 3 levels: (1) words: "Which way is the food from the ant? Count the squares along one straight grid line."; (2) visual: the squares of the first leg are numbered 1, 2, 3 on the grid; (3) almost the answer: the tool moves the ant along the first leg and writes it: "Now tap the other arrow for the next leg."
- Edge cases: a move off the grid gives "The grid ends here."; Undo goes back square by square.
7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "To get to the laddoos, the ant has to crawl how far, and towards which direction? Each square of the grid is 1 cm." then "To get to the sugar, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction." then "To get to the bread, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction; then ___ cm in the ___ direction." Goal chip: "Laddoos, sugar, bread". Guess: for each food the child fills the blanks and presses Check; the ant then walks the legs written and lands on the food (green) or stops short or over. Success: laddoos 2 cm towards the east; sugar 3 cm in the north direction; bread 3 cm in the west direction, then 2 cm in the south direction, 5 cm in all. Why lines: "2 squares of 1 cm each are 2 cm, and the laddoos are on the side of E." "3 squares up are 3 cm, and up is north." "3 cm west, then 2 cm south: 3 + 2 = 5 cm."
- Star Challenge 2 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "To get to the apple, the ant needs to crawl ___ cm towards ___, and then ___ cm towards ___, and finally ___ cm towards ___." then "Identify other routes to reach the point where apple is located. Which one is the shortest?" Goal chip: "The apple routes". Guess: the child fills the six blanks and presses Check. Success: 5 cm towards south, 3 cm towards east, and finally 2 cm towards north: 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm in all, saved as "Route 1, 10 cm". The child builds up to 2 other routes to the apple and saves them; the tool reads each, for example 3 cm east then 3 cm south, 3 + 3 = 6 cm; 1 cm south, 3 cm east, then 2 cm south, 1 + 3 + 2 = 6 cm. The child taps the route they think is shortest and presses Check; a route of 6 cm turns green. Why line: "The apple is 3 cm east and 3 cm south of the ant. The shortest routes go only east and south, and are 6 cm. Your routes may differ."
- End screen (confetti once): "Well done!" Remember: "Each square is 1 cm. Count the squares to find the distance and say the direction." "A path with turns is one leg after another." "The shortest route goes only towards the food." Think and talk: "Can a route with many turns be as short as a route with one turn? When?" Button: "Start again".
8. Assets and Language
- Images: pale paper with the grid (code); a brown ant (top-view cut-out); photo-style cut-outs of a honey jar, cake slice, jam jar, laddoos, sugar cubes, bread and a red apple; the red dashed trail (code); the compass card. English.

media.context: Concept image for Distance and Direction on a Grid. It follows the idea of the ant's grid in your maths book (squares of 1 cm, a compass, an ant crawling along the grid lines) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example, not the numbers of the book's questions.
media.composition: A tall grid on the left with the anthill and the ant near its middle and three foods on its edges, each reached by a coloured arrow with a length pill; a panel on the right that says each path in words, a compass card and the key that one square is 1 cm.
media.description: A grid of 1 cm squares with an ant at its anthill, a leaf 4 cm to the west, a seed 6 cm to the south and a berry reached by 2 cm to the east and then 4 cm to the north.

content.text:
1. Predict first: a berry is 4 cm to the east and 3 cm to the north of the ant. The ant can go east first or north first, or even wander a little. Which routes along the grid lines are the shortest?
2. Route 1: crawl 4 cm towards the east, then 3 cm towards the north. The length is 4 + 3 = 7 cm.
3. Route 2: crawl 3 cm towards the north, then 4 cm towards the east. The length is 3 + 4 = 7 cm. The same length, in a different order.
4. Route 3: crawl 5 cm towards the east, then 3 cm towards the north, then 1 cm towards the west. The length is 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 cm. The step towards the west is a step the wrong way, and it adds length.
5. The shortest routes are 7 cm. They go only towards the berry, east and north, and never west or south.
6. Turns do not decide the length. Try 2 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm east, then 2 cm north. It has three turns. Its length is 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 7 cm, so it is a shortest route too. Count the cm, not the turns.
7. Rule: the shortest route goes only towards the food. A step the wrong way adds to the length.

Worked example: A berry is 4 cm to the east and 3 cm to the north of the ant. Route 1: 4 cm east, then 3 cm north. Route 2: 3 cm north, then 4 cm east. Route 3: 5 cm east, then 3 cm north, then 1 cm west. Find the length of each route. Which routes are the shortest?
1. Route 1 has two legs, 4 cm east and 3 cm north. Length: 4 + 3 = 7 cm.
2. Route 2 has two legs, 3 cm north and 4 cm east. Length: 3 + 4 = 7 cm.
3. Route 3 has three legs, 5 cm east, 3 cm north and 1 cm west. Length: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 cm.
4. Routes 1 and 2 are both 7 cm. Route 3 is 9 cm, which is 2 cm longer.
5. Route 3 goes 1 cm towards the west, away from the berry, and so it also needs 1 cm more towards the east. These two extra steps make the 2 cm.
6. Check: the berry is 4 cm east and 3 cm north, and 4 + 3 = 7. A route that goes only east and north cannot be shorter than 7 cm.
Answer: Routes 1 and 2 are 7 cm and are the shortest. Route 3 is 9 cm, because it goes 1 cm the wrong way

content.question_tex: To get to the sugar, the ant has to crawl $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}\text{ cm}$ in the $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$ direction.
content.publication_text: To get to the sugar, the ant has to crawl $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}\text{ cm}$ in the $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$ direction.

content.text:
1. Each square of the grid is $1\text{ cm}$. Start at the ant.
2. The sugar is straight above the ant, on the same grid line. Count the squares up to the sugar: $3$ squares, so $3\text{ cm}$.
3. Look at the compass. $N$ is at the top, so up is north.
4. The ant crawls $3\text{ cm}$ in the north direction.
5. Check: $3$ squares of $1\text{ cm}$ each are $3\text{ cm}$, and the arrow on the route points up, towards $N$.
Answer: $3\text{ cm}$ in the north direction.

content.question_tex: To get to the bread, the ant has to crawl $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}\text{ cm}$ in the $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$ direction; then $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}\text{ cm}$ in the $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$ direction.
content.publication_text: To get to the bread, the ant has to crawl $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}\text{ cm}$ in the $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$ direction; then $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}\text{ cm}$ in the $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$ direction.

content.text:
1. The bread is not on the same line as the ant, so the route has two legs and turns once.
2. First leg: count the squares from the ant to the corner of the route on the left: $3$ squares, so $3\text{ cm}$. The left side is the side of $W$, so the direction is west.
3. Second leg: at the corner the ant turns and crawls down to the bread: $2$ squares, so $2\text{ cm}$. Down is the side of $S$, so the direction is south.
[Image: Anthill in the Zoo: Ans2: solution]
4. The whole path is $3\text{ cm}$ west, then $2\text{ cm}$ south. Its length is $3 + 2 = 5\text{ cm}$.
5. Check: the two legs are $3$ squares and $2$ squares, and $3 + 2 = 5$ squares of $1\text{ cm}$ each.
Answer: $3\text{ cm}$ in the west direction; then $2\text{ cm}$ in the south direction, $5\text{ cm}$ in all.
[Image: Anthill in the Zoo: Ans2: solution (continued)]

content.text:
1. The route to the apple is drawn with three legs, so it turns twice.
2. First leg: count the squares down the grid line from the ant to the corner at the bottom: $5$ squares, so $5\text{ cm}$ towards south.
3. Second leg: at the corner the ant turns and crawls to the right: $3$ squares, so $3\text{ cm}$ towards east.
[Image: Anthill in the Zoo: Ans3: solution]
4. Third leg: it turns again and crawls up to the apple: $2$ squares, so $2\text{ cm}$ towards north.
5. Length of the whole route: $5 + 3 + 2 = 10\text{ cm}$.
6. Check: south $5\text{ cm}$, east $3\text{ cm}$, north $2\text{ cm}$. The three legs are $5$, $3$ and $2$ squares of $1\text{ cm}$ each.
Answer: $5\text{ cm}$ towards south, $3\text{ cm}$ towards east, and finally $2\text{ cm}$ towards north, $10\text{ cm}$ in all.
[Image: Anthill in the Zoo: Ans3: solution (continued)]

content.publication_text: Identify other routes to reach the point where apple is located. Which one is the shortest?

content.text:
1. Find where the apple is. It is $3$ squares to the right of the ant and $3$ squares below it: $3\text{ cm}$ towards the east and $3\text{ cm}$ towards the south.
2. Route $1$: $3\text{ cm}$ towards east, then $3\text{ cm}$ towards south. Length: $3 + 3 = 6\text{ cm}$.
3. Route $2$: $3\text{ cm}$ towards south, then $3\text{ cm}$ towards east. Length: $3 + 3 = 6\text{ cm}$.
[Image: Anthill in the Zoo: Ans4: solution]
4. Route $3$: $1\text{ cm}$ towards south, $3\text{ cm}$ towards east, then $2\text{ cm}$ towards south. Length: $1 + 3 + 2 = 6\text{ cm}$.
5. The route drawn in your maths book is $5\text{ cm}$ south, $3\text{ cm}$ east and $2\text{ cm}$ north. Length: $5 + 3 + 2 = 10\text{ cm}$.
6. The shortest routes are the $6\text{ cm}$ routes. They go only east and south. The $10\text{ cm}$ route has a step towards the north, away from the apple.
7. Check: any route made of $3\text{ cm}$ east and $3\text{ cm}$ south, in any order, is $6\text{ cm}$. Your answer may differ.
Answer: Sample answer: $3\text{ cm}$ east then $3\text{ cm}$ south, or $3\text{ cm}$ south then $3\text{ cm}$ east. Each is $6\text{ cm}$, a shortest route. Your answer may differ.

media.title: Zoo Grid Locator

tool_config.idea: Read the position of a place on a grid as two numbers, the column first and the row second, by walking a marker east from 0 and then north, and see that swapping the two numbers gives a different place.
tool_config.title: Zoo Grid Locator
tool_config.screen: The zoo grid board on the trip desk, drawn as a warm 3D isometric scene with soft shadows and gentle animation. A friendly wooden desk holds one large board: the zoo map of your maths book on a grid of 12 columns and 12 rows, with the lines numbered 1 to 12 along the bottom and up the left side, 0 at the bottom left corner and the ZOO sign at the bottom. The map is the largest thing on screen. The animals stand at their places as in your maths book: the parrot, flamingo, toucan, giraffe, zebra, big cat, deer, tiger, snake, elephant, lion, monkey, panda, tortoise and crocodile, and the hippo in the pond. A compass card sits beside the map with N at the top, E in red on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left. A round marker starts at 0. An instruction strip at the top shows one sentence in large type, with progress dots under it. Controls: an East step button and a North step button, and each one moves the marker 1 step along the bottom line or up a column line, and if North is tapped first the tool says: First move horizontally from 0, then vertically; tap an animal to read its position; two number boxes labelled column and row to type a pair, with a Go button that moves the marker there; a Swap button that swaps the two numbers of the pair and moves the marker; six dot colours (red, green, blue, orange, black and pink) with a Place dot button and a Remove dot button; Check, Hint, Retry (returns the marker to 0), Reset (clears the dots and returns the marker), Back and Next in the same places on every card. Read-outs: the pair (column,row) with live numbers, the steps counted so far (for example East 8, North 9), and a What is here line that names the animal at the marker or says no animal here. In the dot challenge the What is here line is hidden and the read-out shows only the pair.
feedback: The pair (column,row) changes at once with every step: East changes the first number and North changes the second, for example: You went 1 step east and 4 steps north, so the pair is (1,4).
At each stop the What is here line reads the place, for example: At (8,9) stands the giraffe, or: No animal here.
A typed pair with the numbers in the wrong order moves the marker to the other place and says what is there, for example: (9,8) is 9 steps east and 8 steps north. The giraffe is at (8,9).
A wrong answer on a card shows a soft amber note and never a red cross, for example: Which number is the column? Walk east first. The tool shows the expected pair only after the second try.

A dot on the right meeting point locks in with a soft chime. A dot on another place slides back with a clue, for example: Move east 8 steps first, then north 3 steps. The tool does not say what is at a meeting point in the dot challenge.
tool_config.done_when: The student has walked the marker to the giraffe, read the position of an animal, seen that (9,8) is not the giraffe and that a swapped pair is another place, answered the panda, tortoise and (1,4) questions, named the animals at six positions, written the positions of six animals, and placed the six coloured dots.

placement.where: last concept of the topic, after its teaching and worked examples

challenges: Card 1 (practice values): walk the marker to the giraffe. Tap East 8 times, then North 9 times, and read the pair as it grows. Answer: after 8 steps east the pair is (8,0), and after 9 steps north it is (8,9). The giraffe is at (8,9).
Card 2 (practice values): tap the parrot and read its position. Answer: (1,11), that is 1 step east and 11 steps north.

Card 3 (practice values): type (9,8) in the number boxes and press Go. Is the giraffe there? Answer: no. The tool says no animal here. The giraffe is at (8,9). The first number is the column and the second number is the row.

Card 4 (practice values): tap the big cat and read its position, then press Swap. Answer: the big cat is at (8,7). The swapped pair is (7,8), 7 steps east and 8 steps north, a place on the path with no animal. A pair with its numbers swapped is a different place.

Challenge: 'Start from 0 on the zoo map. How do you reach the panda, and how do we write its position?' Then: 'To reach the tortoise, move ___ steps towards east and reach the ___ column. Then move ___ step(s) ___ and reach the first ___.' Then: 'The location of the tortoise is (4,1). What is at (1,4)?' Then: 'Locate the animal at the following positions on the map. (a) (11,11) ___ (b) (2,6) ___ (c) (6,4) ___ (d) (3,10) ___ (e) (11,3) ___ (f) (10,9) ___' Walk the marker for each one. Answers: the panda: 1 step east to the first column, then 1 step north to the first row, (1,1). The tortoise: 4 steps towards east and reach the 4th column; then 1 step north and reach the first row, (4,1). At (1,4): a snake. Q1: (a) toucan (b) tiger (c) elephant (d) flamingo (e) monkey (f) zebra.

Challenge: 'Write the position of the following animals on the map. (a) Lion ___ (b) Elephant ___ (c) Tortoise ___ (d) Deer ___ (e) Panda ___ (f) Crocodile ___' Tap each animal to read its position. Then: 'Place dots of different colours on the following positions. (a) (8,3) (Red) (b) (2,9) (Green) (c) (7,3) (Blue) (d) (3,8) (Orange) (e) (8,6) (Black) (f) (6,6) (Pink)' Walk the marker to each position and place the dot there. Answers: Q2: (a) lion (3,3) (b) elephant (6,4) (c) tortoise (4,1) (d) deer (10,6) (e) panda (1,1) (f) crocodile (10,1). Q3: red at (8,3), green at (2,9), blue at (7,3), orange at (3,8), black at (8,6), pink at (6,6).

Start at 0. Move east along the bottom to the column, then move north up the column line to the row.
For the giraffe: 8 steps east, then 9 steps north, so the position is (8,9). The first number is the column.
The tool moves the marker 8 steps east for you. Now tap North 9 times and read the pair.

Then move ___ step(s) ___ and reach the first ___.' Then: 'The location of the tortoise is (4,1). What is at (1,4)?' Then: 'Locate the animal at the following positions on the map. (a) (11,11) ___ (b) (2,6) ___ (c) (6,4) ___ (d) (3,10) ___ (e) (11,3) ___ (f) (10,9) ___' Walk the marker for each one. Answers: the panda: 1 step east to the first column, then 1 step north to the first row, (1,1). The tortoise: 4 steps towards east and reach the 4th column; then 1 step north and reach the first row, (4,1). At (1,4): a snake. media.instructions_for_student: The student finds a position on a grid by going east to the column and then north to the row, and sees that the two numbers of a position cannot swap places.
media.description:
A. TOOL TITLE
- Zoo Grid Locator
B. TOOL INFO
- Tool ID: M3.S18.T18.C73.2D1
- Tool type: Concept-activity
- Textbook source: Maps and Locations, Locating the Animals in the Zoological Park (Zoo): the 12 by 12 zoo grid, the panda (1,1), the tortoise (4,1), (1,4), and questions 1, 2 and 3 (developer only). Practice values added here: hippo (6,8), parrot (1,11), big cat (8,7) and (7,8), and the walks to (5,2), (9,5) and (12,8).
C. LEARNING OBJECTIVE
- The student finds a position on a grid by going east to the column and then north to the row, writes it as (column,row), and sees that the order of the two numbers matters.
- Out of scope: negative numbers, other quarters of a grid, distances between positions.
D. TOOL DESCRIPTION
1. Opening Screen
- The zoo map as a grid fills the stage: 12 columns and 12 rows of light green squares with cream paths, trees and a small pond. The vertical lines are numbered 1 to 12 along the bottom and the horizontal lines 1 to 12 up the left side, 0 at the bottom left corner; a wooden "ZOO" sign is at the bottom. Sixteen animals stand where lines meet (panda, tortoise, crocodile, lion, snake, elephant, monkey on a big tree, tiger, deer, big cat, hippo in the pond, giraffe, zebra, flamingo, parrot, toucan). The compass card is in the top right corner. A round orange marker sits at 0.
- Instruction line: "Walk the marker to the hippo. Do you go east first or north first?"
- The child is invited to tap "East first" or "North first".
2. Scene and Objects
- Marker: a round orange pin about one square wide. It moves only along grid lines: first east along the bottom line, then north up a column line, snapping to each line. The numbers it passes light up (columns along the bottom, rows on the left).
- Bracket card "( __ , __ )": the column first, the row second. In Activities 1 and 2 it shows the marker's position live; later it is empty until the child fills it by tapping the number on the bottom line for the column and the number on the left side for the row.
- "What is here" bubble at the marker: the animal's name or "No animal here" (Activities 1 to 3 only). Tapping an animal names it.
- Dot tray (Star Challenge 4): six large dots at the bottom: red, green, blue, orange, black, pink. One goal chip at the top.
3. Main Interaction
- Drag the marker east along the bottom line, then north up a column line. It cannot go up from 0 before going east: it stays and the strip says "First move horizontally from 0, then vertically." Reset goes back to 0.
- Tap a number on a line to put it in the bracket; tap a filled slot to clear it. In Star Challenge 4 tap a dot colour to drop that dot where the marker stands; the marker then hops back to 0.
- Bottom buttons: "Hint", "Reset" and the main button "Check", which becomes "Next" when the goal chip is green. Reset returns the marker to 0 and clears the bracket and dots.
4. Activities
- Activity 1 (guided). Goal line: "Walk the marker to the hippo. East first, then north." Goal chip: "Walk to the hippo". Setup: marker at 0; bracket live; bubble on; the pond glows. Guess: before moving, the child taps "East first" or "North first". Result: the child drags the marker 6 steps east, then 8 steps north; the bracket goes (0,0), (6,0), (6,8) and the bubble says "hippo". Why line: "You went 6 steps east and then 8 steps north, so the hippo is at (6,8)." Help: guided, live bracket and bubble.
- Activity 2 (guided, less help). Goal line: "Find the position of the parrot. Walk to it." Goal chip: "Position of the parrot". Setup: marker at 0; the parrot on the top left tree pulses. Guess: before walking, the child taps one of two brackets, "(1,11)" or "(11,1)". Result: the child walks east, then north, to the parrot; the bracket shows (1,11) and the bubble says "parrot". Why line: "1 step east, then 11 steps north: the parrot is at (1,11)." If the child chose (11,1), the marker goes 11 steps east and 1 north, the bubble says "No animal here" and the strip says "The first number is the column: 11 steps east. The parrot is up on the left."
- Activity 3 (independent). Goal line: "The big cat is at (8,7). A friend says it is at (7,8). Walk to (7,8)." Goal chip: "Is it (7,8)?" Setup: the big cat is shown with its bracket (8,7). Guess: before walking, the child taps "Yes, the big cat is there" or "No". Result: the child walks 7 steps east and 8 steps north; the bubble says "No animal here". Why line: "(7,8) is 7 steps east and 8 steps north. The big cat is at (8,7): 8 steps east and 7 steps north. The first number is the column."
- Activity 4, Practice block (independent). Goal line: "Walk to each place and write its position." Goal chip: "3 walks". Setup: three places one after the other, shown as small flags: (5,2), (9,5) and (12,8); bracket and bubble hidden. Guess: for each flag the child walks the marker there, fills the bracket by tapping the column and row numbers, and presses Check. Result: each bracket matches its flag. Why lines: "5 steps east, then 2 steps north: (5,2)." "9 steps east, then 5 steps north: (9,5)." "12 steps east, then 8 steps north: (12,8)." Help: independent.
- Star Challenges: see section 7.
5. Mathematical Understanding
- A place on a grid is told with two numbers. From 0 the child goes east to the column and then north to the row, and sees the bracket grow. (7,8) and (8,7) use the same numbers in another order, so they are two different places.
- The rules to say at the end are the Remember lines of section 7.
6. Feedback and Hints
- Correct: the bracket, dot or animal turns green with a gentle bounce, the marker hops, the strip shows the why line.
- Mistake: north before east -> red strip, small shake: "First move horizontally from 0, then vertically."
- Mistake: numbers in the wrong order (for example (6,10) for the deer at (10,6)) -> "(6,10) is 6 steps east and 10 steps north. Which number is the column? Walk east first." The marker walks to the written place and the bubble says what is there.
- Mistake: counts squares instead of lines -> "The numbers belong to the lines. Count the lines you pass."
- Mistake: Challenge 4, a dot on the wrong place -> it slides back: "Move east 8 steps first, then north 3 steps." (that part's numbers). Challenge 2, a wrong animal -> "Look at where the marker stands. Which animal is on that meeting point?"
- Hint button, 3 levels: (1) words: "Which number comes first, and which way do you walk for it?"; (2) visual: the column line of the place glows from 0 along the bottom, then the row line glows; (3) almost the answer: the marker walks the east part and stops at the column: "Now go north to the row."
- Edge cases: the marker stops at 12 on the bottom line and at 12 up the side; going back is done with Reset.
7. Ending
- Star Challenge 1 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Start from 0 on the zoo map. How do you reach the panda, and how do we write its position?" then "To reach the tortoise, move ___ steps towards east and reach the ___ column. Then move ___ step(s) ___ and reach the first ___." then "The location of the tortoise is (4,1). What is at (1,4)?" Goal chip: "Panda, tortoise, (1,4)". Guess: for the panda the child walks and fills the bracket; for the tortoise the child fills the blanks (a number blank takes the number tapped on a line, a word blank takes the chip "north", "east", "column" or "row"); for (1,4) the child walks and taps the animal found. The child presses Check for each. Success: the panda is at (1,1); the tortoise: 4 steps towards east, the 4th column, 1 step north, the first row; at (1,4) a snake. Why lines: "1 step east to the first column, then 1 step north to the first row: (1,1)." "4 steps east and 1 step north: the tortoise is at (4,1)." "(1,4) is 1 step east and 4 steps north: a snake. It is not the same place as (4,1)."
- Star Challenge 2 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Locate the animal at the following positions on the map. (a) (11,11) ___ (b) (2,6) ___ (c) (6,4) ___ (d) (3,10) ___ (e) (11,3) ___ (f) (10,9) ___" Goal chip: "Name 6 animals". Guess: for each position the child walks the marker from 0 (it hops back to 0 after each one), taps the animal where it stands and presses Check. Success: (a) toucan, (b) tiger, (c) elephant, (d) flamingo, (e) monkey, (f) zebra. Why line, for example: "11 steps east and 11 steps north: a toucan."
- Star Challenge 3 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Write the position of the following animals on the map. (a) Lion ___ (b) Elephant ___ (c) Tortoise ___ (d) Deer ___ (e) Panda ___ (f) Crocodile ___" Goal chip: "Write 6 positions". Guess: for each animal, which pulses, the child fills the bracket with its column and row and presses Check; the marker then walks east and north from 0 to the written position. Success: lion (3,3), elephant (6,4), tortoise (4,1), deer (10,6), panda (1,1), crocodile (10,1). Why line, for example: "3 steps east and 3 steps north: the lion is at (3,3)."
- Star Challenge 4 (independent). Goal line, in the book's words: "Place dots of different colours on the following positions. (a) (8,3) (Red) (b) (2,9) (Green) (c) (7,3) (Blue) (d) (3,8) (Orange) (e) (8,6) (Black) (f) (6,6) (Pink)" Goal chip: "Place 6 dots". Guess: for each position the child walks the marker, taps the colour to drop the dot, and after all six presses Check. Success: red at (8,3), green at (2,9), blue at (7,3), orange at (3,8), black at (8,6), pink at (6,6). Why line, for example: "8 steps east, then 3 steps north: the red dot is at (8,3)."
- End screen (confetti once): "Well done!" Remember: "Start at 0. Go east to the column, then north to the row." "Write the column first and the row second." "The same two numbers in another order are another place." Think and talk: "Is (3,5) the same place as (5,3)? How do you know?" Button: "Start again".
8. Assets and Language
- Images: the zoo map as a code-drawn 12 by 12 grid (numbered lines, light green ground, cream paths, a small blue pond, a wooden ZOO sign); flat cut-outs of the sixteen animals; the orange marker pin; six coloured dots; the compass card. English.

media.teaching_notes: Predict first: the zoo map is drawn on a grid with a number on every line. To find the giraffe you start at 0. Do you walk east first or north first? Each vertical line is a column and each horizontal line is a row, and every line has a number. The numbers belong to the lines, and an animal stands where a column line and a row line meet. Start at 0, the corner at the bottom left. First move horizontally towards the east along the bottom, counting the column lines, until you reach column 8. That is 8 steps east. Then move vertically towards the north, counting the row lines, until you reach row 9. That is 9 steps north. The giraffe stands at this meeting point. We write the two numbers in a bracket with the column first and the row second: (8,9). In the same way the meeting point of column 1 and row 1 is (1,1). Rule: start at 0, first move east to the column, then north to the row, and write (column,row). 1. Start at 0, the corner at the bottom left of the grid. 2. Move east along the bottom line, counting the numbered column lines 1, 2, 3 up to 8. Stop at column 8. That is 8 steps east. 3. From there move north along the column line, counting the row lines 1, 2, 3 up to 9. Stop at row 9. That is 9 steps north. 4. The giraffe stands where column 8 and row 9 meet. 5. Write the column first and the row second: (8,9). 6. Check: 8 steps east first, then 9 steps north, and the bracket (8,9) lists the column and then the row. Answer: The giraffe is at (8,9): 8 steps east, then 9 steps north

content.text:
1. Predict first: the zoo map is drawn on a grid with a number on every line. To find the giraffe you start at 0. Do you walk east first or north first?
2. Each vertical line is a column and each horizontal line is a row, and every line has a number. The numbers belong to the lines, and an animal stands where a column line and a row line meet.
3. Start at 0, the corner at the bottom left. First move horizontally towards the east along the bottom, counting the column lines, until you reach column 8. That is 8 steps east.
4. Then move vertically towards the north, counting the row lines, until you reach row 9. That is 9 steps north. The giraffe stands at this meeting point.
5. We write the two numbers in a bracket with the column first and the row second: (8,9). In the same way the meeting point of column 1 and row 1 is (1,1).
6. Rule: start at 0, first move east to the column, then north to the row, and write (column,row).

content.text:
Worked example: Find the position of the giraffe on the zoo map. Start from 0, move east to the 8th column, then move north to the 9th row. How do we write the position?
1. Start at 0, the corner at the bottom left of the grid.
2. Move east along the bottom line, counting the numbered column lines 1, 2, 3 up to 8. Stop at column 8. That is 8 steps east.
3. From there move north along the column line, counting the row lines 1, 2, 3 up to 9. Stop at row 9. That is 9 steps north.
4. The giraffe stands where column 8 and row 9 meet.
5. Write the column first and the row second: (8,9).
6. Check: 8 steps east first, then 9 steps north, and the bracket (8,9) lists the column and then the row.
Answer: The giraffe is at (8,9): 8 steps east, then 9 steps north

topics.summary: The whole school trip in one walk: finding east by the rising Sun, directions on a picture and from where you stand, turning right and left on a street map, the metro map with its lines and interchanges, a map with a key, distance and direction on a grid, the shortest route and the position of a place by its column and row.

content.text:
1. Predict first: you have taken the whole school trip. Can you say one idea from each stop, from the rising Sun to the zoo? Read the lines below and tick each idea you remembered.
2. Finding directions: face the rising Sun and you face east. Your left hand points north, your right hand points south, and west is behind you.
3. Check: if you face north, which hand points east? The right hand, and the left hand points west.
4. Directions on a picture: with a compass, N is at the top, S at the bottom, E on the right and W on the left. If a swing is at the top left and a slide at the top right, the slide is east of the swing.
5. Check: the swing is west of the slide. If A is east of B, then B is west of A.
6. Directions from where you stand: the direction of a thing is said from a person or a place. A girl stands at the centre of a room. A table above her is north of her. A bed on her right is east. A door below her is south. A cupboard on her left is west.
7. Check: from the bed, the girl is to the west.
8. Street map: a map shows roads and places seen from above, the compass shows north, and a dotted line shows a route. A right turn takes north to east, east to south, south to west and west to north. A left turn goes the other way round.
9. Check: a cycle drives north, turns left and turns left again. It drives west and then south. The bus that drives north and turns right drives east, and a second right turn makes it drive south.
10. Metro map: coloured lines are different routes and a circle is a station. A capsule with two coloured dots is an interchange, where you can change from one line to the other. Where two lines cross without a capsule, you cannot change lines.
11. Check: count the circles between two stations and do not count the two ends. A capsule counts as one station. Hauz Khas to Kalkaji Mandir has 4 stations between. Kalkaji Mandir to Badarpur has 6. So there are 4 + 1 + 6 = 11 stations between Hauz Khas and Badarpur. The 1 is Kalkaji Mandir, where you change lines.
12. Making a map: a map uses symbols, and the key says what each symbol means. Mark a hidden thing with a red dot.
13. Check: in a library corner, a long rectangle can be a shelf and a square with 4 small squares a table with 4 chairs. Every symbol on the map must be in the key.
14. Distance and direction on a grid: each square is 1 cm. Count the squares for the distance and say the direction. A path with turns is a list of legs.
15. Check: 2 cm towards the east, then 4 cm towards the north is 2 + 4 = 6 cm.
16. Shortest route: it goes only towards the food. A berry 4 cm east and 3 cm north is 4 + 3 = 7 cm away along the lines. A route with a step 1 cm the wrong way is longer: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 cm.
17. Check: the apple of your maths book is 3 cm east and 3 cm south of the ant. A shortest route is 3 + 3 = 6 cm. The route drawn there is 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm, so it is not the shortest.
18. Position on a grid: start at 0, move east to the column, then north to the row, and write (column,row). The giraffe is 8 steps east and 9 steps north, so it is at (8,9). The panda is at (1,1) and the tortoise is at (4,1).
19. Check: (9,8) is another place, because the column comes first. The first number is the steps east.
20. Which stop would you like to try again? Pick one idea and say its rule aloud.

objectives.objective_text: Students find east by facing the rising Sun and name the direction of the left hand, the right hand and behind using the four directions of the compass.
Students write the direction Manu faces and the directions of his left hand and right hand when he faces the rising Sun, and say which way is west.
Students say which object is north, south, east or west of another object on a picture with a compass, reading the top of the picture as north and the right as east.
Students write the direction of things in a room from a girl standing at the centre, and say that if one thing is east of another then the other is west of it.

Students use clues about directions to colour four tents, draw a tent east of the lake, write the direction of things in a room from the girl, and name things in the four directions of their own room.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students read a street map from above, use the compass to say which place is north, south, east or west of another place, and follow a dotted route along named roads.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students say the direction a bus or a cycle is driving after each right turn or left turn, starting from north, east, south or west, and name the road it turns onto.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students name the roads, turns and directions of the bus route on the street map, and find houses and stops by reading the map and the compass.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students read the key of a metro map, name what the coloured lines, the circle and the capsule mean, and find the stations where two lines meet.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students count the stations between two stations on a metro map, count an interchange capsule as one station, and change lines only at a capsule where the two lines meet.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students trace routes on the metro map between two stations, mark stations on their lines, count the stations between, and say which route has the fewest stations and where to change lines.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students make a map of a place seen from above, draw a key that explains each symbol, and mark a hidden thing with a red dot.

objectives.strand_name: Street Maps, Metro Maps and Keys
objectives.objective_text: Students make a map of their school with a key for every symbol, hide objects and mark them with red dots, and write a clue that tells a friend how to find one.
Students count the squares of a grid along a straight line to find a distance in cm, name its direction, and write a path with a turn as two legs.
Students compare routes to the same point on a grid by adding the cm of their legs, and name the shortest route as the one with no step the wrong way.
Students trace the path of the ant on the grid to the laddoos, the sugar, the bread and the apple, say each leg as cm and a direction, and find the shortest route to the apple.
Students find the position of a place on a grid by moving east from 0 to its column and then north to its row, and write it as (column,row).
Students explain why the order of the two numbers in a position matters, and tell (8,9) from (9,8) by saying how many steps east and how many steps north each one is.
Students walk east and then north on the zoo grid to find the animal at a position, write the position of an animal, and mark positions with coloured dots.

video_coverage.book_item: Book item: Manu is facing the rising Sun. That direction is ___. His left hand is pointing in the ___ direction. His right hand is pointing in the ___ direction.
Book item: Which way is west?

Book item: Children are at a bird-watching camp. Read the clues and colour the tents in the camp accordingly. The tent to the west of the road is blue. The tent closest to the lake is green. The tent north of the green tent is purple. The tent south of the lake is yellow.
Book item: Now, draw a tent to the east of the lake.
Book item: Write the directions of the following in relation to the girl. Window ___ Bed ___ Cupboard ___ Bedside table ___

Book item: Make a drawing of your room and locate the direction in which different things have been placed in relation to you standing at the centre of the room. Make the direction arrow for your room.
Book item: Write the names of the things that are placed in the following directions. East ___ West ___ North ___ South ___
Book item: The bus will start from the parking area. It will go north and then it will take a right turn onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction to reach Stop 1 (S1).
Book item: To reach Stop 2 (S2), it will turn ___ (right/left) onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction.
Book item: Whose houses are situated to the east of Jaideep's house? ___
Book item: Mark the route from Ravi's house to the children's park.
Book item: Which stop is closer to Lali's house? ___
Book item: Golu is running late. Trace the route to help him reach the nearest bus stop.
Book item: In which direction would Prem have to move to reach Stop 2?
Book item: What do the different coloured lines represent?
Book item: Mark the Qutb Minar station on the Yellow Line and the Supreme Court station on the Blue Line.
Book item: Look at the metro map and trace different routes from the Qutb Minar metro station to the Supreme Court metro station.

Book item: Lali says, "We can take the Yellow Line and change the metro at Hauz Khas to take the Magenta Line." If the children follow Lali's suggestion, at which station(s) do they need to change the metro line again to reach the Supreme Court metro station?
Book item: Which route has the least number of stations between Qutb Minar and Supreme Court?
Book item: Which metro route(s), do you think, is/are the best way to reach the zoo from Qutb Minar? ___

Book item: Make a map showing the different places in your school. Make a key for the symbols used in the map. Hide some objects in these places. Mark the positions where things are hidden with red dots or flags. Now, challenge your friends to find the hidden things by reading the map.
Book item: To get to the laddoos, the ant has to crawl how many cm, and towards which direction?
Book item: To get to the sugar, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction.
Book item: To get to the bread, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction; then ___ cm in the ___ direction.
Book item: To get to the apple, the ant needs to crawl ___ cm towards ___, and then ___ cm towards ___, and finally ___ cm towards ___.
Book item: Identify other routes to reach the point where apple is located. Which one is the shortest?
Book item: Start from 0 on the zoo map. How do you reach the panda, and how do we write its position?
Book item: To reach the tortoise, move ___ steps towards east and reach the ___ column. Then move ___ step(s) ___ and reach the first ___.
Book item: The location of the tortoise is (4,1). What is at (1,4)?
Book item: Locate the animal at the following positions on the map. (a): (11,11) ___; (b): (2,6) ___; (c): (6,4) ___; (d): (3,10) ___; (e): (11,3) ___; (f): (10,9) ___
Book item: Write the position of the following animals on the map. (a): Lion ___; (b): Elephant ___; (c): Tortoise ___; (d): Deer ___; (e): Panda ___; (f): Crocodile ___
Book item: Place dots of different colours on the following positions. (a): (8,3) (Red); (b): (2,9) (Green); (c): (7,3) (Blue); (d): (3,8) (Orange); (e): (8,6) (Black); (f): (6,6) (Pink)

chapter_approach.intro: The chapter follows one school trip. It starts with a bird that finds its way and a child who faces the rising Sun, then reads the camp, a room, a street map with a bus route, a metro map, an ant's grid and the animals of a zoo. A short video explains each idea, and an interactive tool lets the student try it alone.

points.text: Every idea has one short concept video. The tool that follows is where the student explores, steers, counts and checks the idea alone, with hints, retry and reset. Six tools, each with its own purpose, follow the chapter's own plan.
points.title: Videos teach, tools explore

points.text: Each tool opens with a short recall of the video idea, then lets the student play and apply it, and ends with the chapter's own questions, used exactly as the book gives them.
points.title: A tool in three steps

points.text: Every solved example and every answerable question of the book is its own short video with a step by step solution and a question picture and a solution picture, in a Questions topic that follows the idea it practises.
points.title: Every book question has its own video

points.text: Compass roses, street maps, the metro map, the ant's grid and the zoo grid carry each idea. The compass is the same on every board: N at the top, E in red on the right.
points.title: The picture is the mathematics

points.text: Roads, stops, metro lines, grid sizes and the places of animals and foods are the book's own. Any number the plan adds is a practice value and is said to be one.
points.title: Only the book's pictures and numbers
